definition_zh: 久坐的；不活动的；固定的、不迁徙的（部落）；需要久坐的（工作）
definition_en: involving a lot of sitting and little exercise, or staying in one place instead of moving about
core_image: 一个人一整天几乎不离椅子，身体像被钉在了座位上
scene: 学生备考常常整天坐在书桌前，体育老师提醒他们每隔一小时起身伸展。Her sedentary routine made her back ache by the end of the term.
sceneCN: 这里 sedentary 是「久坐的；缺乏活动的」（第 1 个义项：长时间坐着、活动很少）；句意：她久坐的生活方式让整个学期结束时后背一直疼。

pos.zh: 固定的；不迁徙的（部落、民族）

derivatives.zh: 由 sedentary 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「久坐性；定居不迁徙的状态」
由 sedentary 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「以久坐的方式；定居不动地」
与 sedentary 同源的学术名词，指人类由游居转为定居的生活方式
与 sedentary 同源的动词，义为「使由游牧转为定居」

senses.title: Spending long hours seated and inactive
senses.definition: spending most of the time sitting down with little physical movement
senses.definitionCN: 大部分时间坐着，身体活动很少
senses.example: Long hours of sedentary study weakened his back.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间久坐学习使他的背部变得虚弱。
senses.why: The Latin verb sedere means to sit, and someone who sits all day has almost no motion left in the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 sedere 意为坐下，一整天坐着的人，词里几乎不剩任何动作。

senses.title: Staying fixed in one place
senses.definition: living in one settled place rather than moving with herds or seasons
senses.definitionCN: 长期住在固定地点，而不是随牲畜或季节迁移
senses.example: Sedentary tribes built granaries and stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 定居部落修建了粮仓和石墙。
senses.why: Anthropology takes the single detail of sitting down and turns it into a whole way of life: the camp becomes a village.
senses.whyCN: 人类学抓住「坐下来」这一个细节，把它扩展为一整套生活方式：营地变成了村落。

senses.title: Of a job done at a desk
senses.definition: describing work or duties that force a person to remain seated for most of the day
senses.definitionCN: 形容要求人一天大部分时间保持坐着的工作或职责
senses.example: Clerical jobs are often extremely sedentary.
senses.exampleCN: 文职工作往往极其久坐。
senses.why: Once sedentary names a habit, it can also name the occupation that forces the habit on a worker.
senses.whyCN: sedentary 一旦指一种习惯，也就可以指强迫工作者养成这种习惯的职业。

senses.title: Medical tone for a bad habit
senses.titleCN: 医学语体中的久坐（健康风险）
senses.definition: used in health writing to frame a sitting-rich routine as a health risk
senses.definitionCN: 在健康类文章中，把大量坐着的日常安排视为健康风险
senses.example: The clinic warns that a sedentary lifestyle raises heart risk.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所警告说久坐的生活方式会增加心脏风险。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the calm Latin word for sitting and uses it to fence off the modern habit it dislikes.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个平静的拉丁词「坐」，用它来圈定它不喜欢的现代习惯。

senses.title: Plants and animals that do not travel
senses.definition: describing organisms that stay rooted or attached in one spot
senses.definitionCN: 形容扎在或附着在同一个地点、不移动的生物
senses.example: Corals are sedentary animals that barely change site.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚是几乎不会更换地点的固着动物。
senses.why: Biology widens the human idea of sitting still to any creature that does not move from its spot.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把人类「坐着不动」的概念扩展到任何不离开原地的生物。

senses.title: Literary use for sitting figures
senses.titleCN: 端坐的；坐着不动的（书面描写）
senses.definition: used in older writing to describe a seated posture or figure
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的书面语中形容坐着的姿态或身姿
senses.example: The old portrait shows her in a sedentary pose.
senses.exampleCN: 旧画像中她呈端坐的姿态。
senses.why: Earlier writers used sedentary to describe the act of sitting rather than the lack of exercise.
senses.whyCN: 较早的作者用 sedentary 描写坐着这一动作本身，而不是缺乏锻炼。

intro.en: Sedentary comes from Latin sedentarius, from the verb sedere, to sit, through the past participle sedentem.
intro.cn: sedentary 来自拉丁语 sedentarius，源自动词 sedere（坐）的现在分词词干 sedentem。

items.en: Sedere means to sit, from a reconstructed Indo-European root meaning to stay in one place.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐，其源头一般重构为表示「停留原地」的印欧语词根。

items.en: Sedes is a seat or dwelling, and sedentarius describes people who stay settled.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语中 sedes 指座位或居所，sedentarius 形容固定居住的人。

items.en: Medieval and Renaissance Latin use sedentarius for tribes that do not wander.
items.cn: 中世纪与文艺复兴拉丁语用 sedentarius 指不游动的部落。

items.en: English borrows the word first for settled peoples and posts.
items.cn: 英语先借入该词，用来描述定居的族群与固定岗位。

items.en: Medicine links the word with desk work and lack of exercise.
items.cn: 现代早期至十九世纪，医学把该词与伏案工作、缺少锻炼联系起来。

items.en: Sedentary is now the standard word for screen-bound desk life.
items.cn: 如今 sedentary 已成为描述屏幕前伏案生活的标准词。

note.en: Sedentary belongs to the Latin sitting family of sedere and sits close to words for still, restful, and inactive lives.
note.cn: sedentary 属于拉丁语 sedere「坐」这一词族，并与表示静止、休息与不活动的词相邻。

entries.definition: in a way that involves much sitting
entries.definitionCN: 以久坐的方式

entries.definition: the quality of sitting much and moving little
entries.definitionCN: 久坐不动的状态

entries.definition: calm and unhurried, or to make calm with a drug
entries.definitionCN: 平静从容的；用药使镇静

entries.definition: the practice of living in permanent settlements
entries.definitionCN: 定居生活方式（源自同一词根的学术词）

entries.definition: not moving or working as usual
entries.definitionCN: 不活动的；闲置的

entries.definition: not moving from a position
entries.definitionCN: 静止的；不移动的

entries.definition: slow in movement or response
entries.definitionCN: 迟缓的；懒散的

entries.definition: having to stay at a desk for work
entries.definitionCN: 困在办公桌前的

normalIntro.en: Sedentary keeps the Latin verb sedere, to sit, inside it: the whole word is a chair.
normalIntro.cn: sedentary 内部保留着拉丁语动词 sedere「坐」：整词就是一把椅子。

normal.en: Sed- is the sit root, the same one hiding in sediment, things that settle down.
normal.cn: sed- 是「坐」的词根，sediment（沉积物）里也藏着它，沉积物就是沉下来的东西。

normal.en: Health reports pair sedentary with lifestyle, behaviour, and risk.
normal.cn: 健康报道常把 sedentary 与 lifestyle、behaviour、risk 搭配。

normal.en: Anthropology pairs sedentary with tribes and settlements, the opposite of nomadic.
normal.cn: 人类学把 sedentary 与 tribes、settlements 搭配，是 nomadic 的反面。

normal.en: Sedentary work is the most common collocation in job adverts.
normal.cn: sedentary work 是招聘广告里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Compare stationary: stationary means not moving, sedentary means spending the day sitting.
normal.cn: 对比 stationary：stationary 指不移动，sedentary 指整日坐着。

abstract.en: Picture a grey office chair with a person shaped dent that never leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一把灰色办公椅，上面留着一个人形凹陷，始终没人离开。

abstract.en: Imagine a village built where a herd of cattle once stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象在牛群曾经停留的地方建起了一座村庄。

abstract.en: Think of a smart watch buzzing, urging its owner to stand up.
abstract.cn: 想想一只智能手表震动报警，催促主人站起来。

examples.en: The doctor blamed his sedentary habits for the weight gain.
examples.cn: 医生把体重上升归因于他久坐的习惯。

examples.en: Sedentary settlements grew up around the first farms.
examples.cn: 定居点在最早的农田周围逐渐形成。

examples.en: Office workers often need a reminder to move after a sedentary afternoon.
examples.cn: 办公室职员在久坐的下午之后往往需要有人提醒他们动一动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛登特瑞」——比赛登上特设的椅子，一整天坐着不下来，就是 sedentary；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ 现在分词词干 sedent- → sedentarius（常坐的、定居的）→ 英语 sedentary，核心义「长时间坐着的」。

sensesIntro.en: Sedentary starts from the simple act of sitting and grows into a settled way of life, a kind of job, a health warning, and finally a biological state.
sensesIntro.cn: sedentary 从「坐着」这一简单动作出发，扩展为定居的生活方式、一类工作、健康警示，最后落到生物的固着状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that stays in the chair while the rest of the room moves on.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋里其他一切都在动，只有一具身体留在椅子上。

branches.en: The plain health sense is hours of sitting with little movement.
branches.cn: 基本义就是长时间坐着、活动很少。

branches.en: A people that sits in one spot settles into villages.
branches.cn: 在一地「坐定」的人群就定居成了村落。

branches.en: The job and the medical warning both grow from long hours at a desk.
branches.cn: 工作需要久坐，医学警示也从伏案时长而生。

branches.en: Any organism attached to one spot is sedentary in the same way.
branches.cn: 任何附着在一处的生物都以同样方式「久坐」。

branches.en: Both keep the literal picture of a seated body.
branches.cn: 两者都保留着身体坐着的字面画面。

intro.en: Sedentary is a Latin sitting root with a classical adjective ending, joined by English sit, sediment, and session.
intro.cn: sedentary 是拉丁语「坐」词根加古典形容词词尾，与英语 sit、sediment、session 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit, and sedentarius means seated or settled.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，sedentarius 意为坐着的、定居的。

items.example: Sedere gives the core idea of the family.
items.exampleCN: sedere 提供这个词族的核心概念。

items.example: Sedes is the seat behind the settled sense.
items.exampleCN: sedes 是「定居」义背后的座位。

items.example: Sedentarius is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: sedentarius 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ary keeps the Latin shape on English soil.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 让该词在英语里保留拉丁语形态。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sedentariness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 sedentariness。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sedentarily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 sedentarily。

items.meaning: matter that settles at the bottom
items.example: Sediment shows the same root from sedere.
items.exampleCN: sediment 显示了来自 sedere 的同一词根。

items.meaning: a meeting where people sit together
items.example: Session shares the sitting image.
items.exampleCN: session 共享「坐」的意象。

items.example: Sedate is a calm cousin of sedentary.
items.exampleCN: sedate 是 sedentary 气质平静的近亲。

definition_zh: 引诱；诱惑；勾引；诱使（某人做某事）
definition_en: to persuade someone to do something they would not usually do, often by charm, flattery, or temptation
core_image: 一只手把闪亮的东西举到你眼前，牵着你离开原路
scene: 广告里的度假照片阳光灿烂，她本来只想看看，最后却订了一张机票。The glossy brochure seduced her into booking a holiday she could hardly afford.
sceneCN: 这里 seduce 是「诱使；诱惑」（第 2 个义项：用魅力或好处让人做出本不会做的事）；句意：那本精美的宣传册诱惑她预订了一场她几乎负担不起的度假。

derivatives.zh: 由 seduce 加名词后缀 -tion，义为「引诱；诱惑；诱惑物」
由 seduce 加表示人的后缀 -er，义为「引诱者；诱惑者」
由 seduce 加形容词后缀 -ive，义为「诱人的；有诱惑力的」
由 seductive 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「诱人地；以诱惑的方式」

senses.title: To draw someone into a sexual relationship
senses.definition: to persuade someone into a sexual relationship, now usually with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 引诱他人与自己发生性关系，今天多带贬义
senses.example: The film shows a nobleman trying to seduce the maid.
senses.exampleCN: 影片中一位贵族试图勾引女仆。
senses.why: The Latin prefix se- means aside and ducere means to lead, so seducing is leading someone aside, away from the expected path.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 se- 意为「向旁边」，ducere 意为「带领」，所以 seduce 就是把某人带向一旁、带离原本该走的路。

senses.title: To tempt someone into a choice
senses.definition: to persuade someone to do something, often something they will later regret
senses.definitionCN: 劝说某人去做某事，往往是一件事后会后悔的事
senses.example: Praise may seduce a young player into losing focus.
senses.exampleCN: 赞扬可能诱使年轻球员失去专注。
senses.why: Once the idea of leading aside is in place, any tempting offer can do the leading, not only another person.
senses.whyCN: 「带向一旁」的意象一旦成立，任何诱人的提议都能充当那只带路的手，而不只是另一个人。

senses.title: Of products and ideas that tempt
senses.definition: to make someone want something strongly, used of goods, offers, or promises
senses.definitionCN: 让某人强烈想要某物，用于商品、优惠或承诺
senses.example: Low prices seduce shoppers into buying twice as much.
senses.exampleCN: 低价诱使顾客多买一倍的东西。
senses.why: Advertising performs the leading aside: the shiny object acts like a voice calling the buyer away from the aisle.
senses.whyCN: 广告在做「带向一旁」这件事：亮眼的商品像在喊，把顾客从原本的货架旁引开。

senses.title: To argue someone over by charm
senses.definition: to win a person over to a view by charm rather than force or proof
senses.definitionCN: 靠魅力而非武力或论证把某人争取到某一观点一边
senses.example: A silver voice seduced the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 一副动听的嗓音把整个委员会都说动了。
senses.why: In older English the verb often meant simply winning a person over, and that polite sense survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 较早的英语中这个动词常只表示「争取到某人」，这一客气涵义仍在正式书面语中留存。

senses.title: To draw a person away from duty
senses.titleCN: 使变节；引诱离开（职守、立场）
senses.definition: to lure a person away from loyalty, duty, or a cause they belong to
senses.definitionCN: 把人从忠诚、职守或原本归属的事业中引走
senses.example: Rivals tried to seduce him from his party with a bigger post.
senses.exampleCN: 对手想用一个更高的职位把他诱离本党。
senses.why: The images se- aside and duc- lead keep working here: a rival leads the person aside from the ranks.
senses.whyCN: 「向旁」与「带领」的意象在这里照常起作用：对手把人从队伍中带向一旁。

senses.title: Of technology that quietly pulls attention
senses.definition: to occupy someone so fully that they forget their main occupation
senses.definitionCN: 把人深深吸引住，以致忘记本来的正事
senses.example: The endless feed seduces people into scrolling for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 无休止的信息流诱使人们滚动屏幕数小时。
senses.why: A machine can also lead a person aside, which is why critics now say that phones seduce rather than simply attract.
senses.whyCN: 机器同样能把人带向一旁，所以批评者说手机是「诱走」人，而不只是吸引人。

intro.en: Seduce is built from the Latin prefix se-, meaning aside, and ducere, meaning to lead, through the verb seducere.
intro.cn: seduce 由拉丁语前缀 se-（向旁）与 ducere（带领）构成，源自动词 seducere。

items.en: Ducere means to lead, and the prefix se- carries the idea of aside or apart.
items.cn: ducere 意为带领，前缀 se- 带有「向旁边、分开」的意思。

items.en: Seducere means to lead away or set apart, used of troops splitting off.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语 seducere 意为把东西带走或分开，用于描述部队脱离主力。

items.en: Later writers extend seducere to misleading someone into error.
items.cn: 较晚的作者把 seducere 扩展到引人犯错。

items.en: English seduce first means to lead astray from truth or duty.
items.cn: 英语 seduce 起初指把人从真理或职守上引偏。

items.en: The sexual sense becomes the dominant one in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，与性关系有关的法义逐渐成为主要义项。

items.en: The word spreads to advertising, politics, and social media.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词扩散到广告、政治与社交媒体。

note.en: Seduce belongs to the leading family of Latin ducere and sits close to the family of tempting and luring verbs.
note.cn: seduce 属于拉丁语 ducere「带领」这一词族，并与表示诱惑与引诱的动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of persuading someone to do something by charm
entries.definitionCN: 用魅力说服别人的行为；诱惑

entries.definition: very attractive and tempting
entries.definitionCN: 有诱惑力的；诱人的

entries.definition: a person who seduces others
entries.definitionCN: 引诱者；诱惑者

entries.definition: to work out a conclusion by leading the mind from facts
entries.definitionCN: 从事实推出结论（与 seduce 同用 ducere 词根）

entries.definition: to lead or guide an activity
entries.definitionCN: 进行、主持或带领（源自同一词根 ducere）

entries.definition: to make someone want something, often unwisely
entries.definitionCN: 引诱；诱惑（常指不明智之事）

entries.definition: to attract someone into a trap with the promise of good
entries.definitionCN: 以好处相诱把人引入圈套

entries.definition: to attract by offering pleasure or advantage
entries.definitionCN: 引诱；诱惑（多指以好处相诱）

entries.definition: to please and win someone by personality
entries.definitionCN: 以魅力取悦、打动某人

normalIntro.en: Seduce is se- aside plus duc- lead: a word about being led off the road you meant to walk.
normalIntro.cn: seduce 是 se-「向旁」加 duc-「带领」：说的是被人从本该走的路上带开。

normal.en: The duc- root shows in conduct, deduce, and introduce, all with some idea of leading.
normal.cn: duc- 词根见于 conduct、deduce、introduce，都含有带领之意。

normal.en: The usual pattern is seduce someone into doing something.
normal.cn: 最常见的结构是 seduce someone into doing something。

normal.en: The passive be seduced by is common in reporting on ads and offers.
normal.cn: 被动式 be seduced by 在报道广告与优惠时很常见。

normal.en: Seduction and seductive keep the same leading image in different parts of speech.
normal.cn: seduction 与 seductive 在不同词性里保留着同一个带领意象。

normal.en: Compare tempt: tempt is the plain everyday verb, seduce adds charm and a sense of being led away.
normal.cn: 对比 tempt：tempt 是日常平实的动词，seduce 多了魅力与「被带开」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a dancer in a bright hall gently pulling a partner off the dance floor.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮大厅里的舞者轻轻把舞伴拉离舞池。

abstract.en: Imagine a glowing shop sign bending a passer-by to a side street.
abstract.cn: 想象一块发光的店招把路人弯进旁边的小巷。

abstract.en: Think of a phone on a desk lighting up every minute until the essay is left unread.
abstract.cn: 想想桌上每分钟亮一次的的手机，直到那篇论文再也没被翻开。

examples.en: The promise of easy money seduced many small investors.
examples.cn: 轻松赚钱的承诺诱使许多小投资者上了钩。

examples.en: He was seduced by the idea of life on a tropical island.
examples.cn: 他被热带岛屿生活的想法所诱惑。

examples.en: No bonus could seduce her away from the project she loved.
examples.cn: 无论多少奖金都无法把她从她热爱的项目中诱走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞丢斯」——有人把东西「塞」进你手里，又「丢」掉你的坚持，斯文地把你带走，就是 seduce；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 se-（向旁）＋ ducere（带领）→ seducere（带开、分开）→ 英语 seduce，核心义「把人从原路上带向一旁」。

sensesIntro.en: Seduce keeps one shape in every sense: a person is led aside, whether by desire, by an offer, by charm, or by a screen.
sensesIntro.cn: seduce 在各义项中保持同一个形态：一个人被带向一旁，无论诱因是情欲、好处、魅力，还是一块屏幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leading you sideways, away from the path you chose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着你向旁边走，离开你原本选定的路。

branches.en: The sexual sense is the classic case of being led aside.
branches.cn: 与性有关的意义是「被带向一旁」的典型情形。

branches.en: The general sense lets any temptation do the leading.
branches.cn: 一般义让任何诱惑都能充当带路者。

branches.en: Goods and screens now do the pulling that a person once did.
branches.cn: 如今商品与屏幕承担了昔日由人完成的拉扯。

branches.en: Persuasion and disloyalty both move a person out of a group.
branches.cn: 说服与变节都把人带离原属的群体。

branches.en: Both end in a purchase the buyer did not plan.
branches.cn: 两者都以买下一件原本没打算买的东西收尾。

intro.en: Seduce is a Latin prefix and a Latin leading root, with English seduction and seductive built on top.
intro.cn: seduce 是拉丁语前缀加拉丁语「带领」词根，英语在其上构成 seduction 与 seductive。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere means to lead, and seducere means to lead apart or aside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere 意为带领，seducere 意为把东西带开、带向一旁。

items.example: The prefix se- adds the sideways movement.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 se- 加上了横向移动的意思。

items.example: Ducere is the leading root of the family.
items.exampleCN: ducere 是这个词族的「带领」词根。

items.example: Seducere is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: seducere 是直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion forms seduction.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 构成 seduction。

items.example: The suffix -er forms seducer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 seducer。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms seductive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 seductive。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms seductively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 seductively。

items.meaning: to lead back, hence to make smaller
items.example: Reduce lends the prefix re- to the same root.
items.exampleCN: reduce 用前缀 re- 接了同一词根。

items.example: Introduce shows the same leading root.
items.exampleCN: introduce 显示相同的带领词根。

definition_zh: 渗；渗漏；渗透；（液体慢慢）渗出；（想法、情绪悄悄）蔓延
definition_en: to flow or spread slowly through small openings or porous material
core_image: 水一滴一滴穿过布料的孔隙，慢慢洇出一片湿痕
scene: 暴雨过后，雨水顺着墙角慢慢渗进地下室的地面。After the storm, rainwater seeped through the corner wall and spread across the basement floor.
sceneCN: 这里 seep 是「液体慢慢渗过缝隙」（第 1 个义项：液体通过小孔或缝隙缓缓流动）；句意：暴雨过后，雨水顺着墙角慢慢渗进地下室的地面。

pos.zh: （想法、情绪等）不知不觉地蔓延

derivatives.zh: 由动词 seep 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「渗漏、渗出的液体」
由 seep 加 -ing 构成的形容词形式，义为「渗出的、慢慢流出的」
口语或方言中由 seep 加 -y 构成，义为「到处渗水的、潮湿滴水的」

senses.title: To trickle through small openings
senses.definition: to flow slowly through tiny holes, cracks, or porous material
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢地穿过小孔、裂缝或多孔材料流动
senses.example: Rainwater seeps through the cracks in the stone wall.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水透过石墙的裂缝渗进来。
senses.why: The word itself pictures a liquid moving so slowly that you notice where it has already reached, not its movement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的画面就是液体慢到看不出在动，只能看见它已经洇到的地方。

senses.title: To move or spread gradually
senses.definition: to spread slowly and quietly into a place or a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而悄无声息地扩散到某个地方或某群人之中
senses.example: Doubt began to seep into the team after the second defeat.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次失利之后，疑虑开始渗入队伍。
senses.why: The image of liquid entering through cracks is used for anything that enters little by little.
senses.whyCN: 「液体从缝隙渗进来」的画面被用来形容一切一点一点进入的东西。

senses.title: To pass time or quality slowly
senses.definition: to pass or be revealed slowly and unnoticeably
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而不易察觉地流逝或显露出来
senses.example: The afternoon seeped away while we waited for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们等公交车时，下午悄然过去了。
senses.why: Because the flow is slow, the word suggests a sense of quiet loss or gradual appearance.
senses.whyCN: 因为流动极慢，这个词自带一种静静流失、慢慢显露的意味。

senses.title: A slow leak
senses.definition: a small, steady leak, or the place where liquid slowly escapes
senses.definitionCN: 细小的、持续的漏液，或液体慢慢逸出的地方
senses.example: A seep under the boiler had made the floor damp.
senses.exampleCN: 锅炉下面的一处渗漏把地面弄湿了。
senses.why: The verb is also used for the leak itself, especially in technical and geological writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词也被用来指渗漏本身，尤其是在技术文本与地质文本中。

senses.title: Oil or gas rising naturally
senses.definition: oil, gas, or water that rises naturally to the surface from underground
senses.definitionCN: 从地下自然升到地表的石油、天然气或水
senses.example: Geologists mapped an oil seep at the bottom of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家标出了海底的一处石油渗出点。
senses.why: Geology turns the everyday drip into a feature of the ground that can be located and measured.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把日常的滴水现象变成可以定位、可以测量的地下特征。

intro.en: Seep is recorded from about the sixteenth century and probably goes back to an Old English or dialect word for a slow trickle, related to sipe and to dialect soak words.
intro.cn: seep 大约记录于十六世纪，一般认为源自表示「细流、慢慢淌」的古英语或方言词，与 sipe 以及方言中的浸泡类词相关。

items.en: A related word for a slow trickle is likely, but the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示细流的古英语相关词，但确切形式存疑。

items.en: Seep first appears in writing as a verb for liquids moving slowly.
items.cn: seep 首次见于文献，作动词，指液体缓慢流动。

items.en: The noun appears for the leak or the wet place itself.
items.cn: 名词用法出现，指渗漏或渗水的地方。

items.en: Geologists adopt the word for oil and water rising to the surface.
items.cn: 地质学家采用该词，指石油和地下水渗到地表。

items.en: The figurative sense for feelings and ideas spreading slowly becomes common.
items.cn: 表示情感与观念慢慢蔓延的比喻义变得常见。

items.en: Seepage and seepy extend the family in technology and dialect speech.
items.cn: seepage 与 seepy 在技术与方言话语中扩展了这个词族。

note.en: Seep is the slow-member of the leak family, next to soak, sipe, and dripping verbs.
note.cn: seep 是「漏」这个词族里最慢的那个，与 soak、sipe 以及各种滴漏动词相邻。

entries.definition: the slow leaking of liquid
entries.definitionCN: 液体缓慢渗漏

entries.definition: trickling slowly out
entries.definitionCN: 慢慢渗出的

entries.definition: to trickle slowly, used in dialect
entries.definitionCN: （方言）缓缓渗出，一般认为与 seep 同源

entries.definition: to flow in a thin, weak stream
entries.definitionCN: 滴流；细流

entries.definition: to flow out very slowly and thickly
entries.definitionCN: （浓稠液体）慢慢渗出

entries.definition: to let liquid escape through a hole
entries.definitionCN: 漏；渗漏

normalIntro.en: Seep sounds long and soft, like water that has no hurry at all.
normalIntro.cn: seep 的读音又长又轻，像一点都不着急的水。

normal.en: Seep through means to pass slowly through a crack.
normal.cn: seep through 就是慢慢渗过裂缝。

normal.en: Seepage is the noun for water that has seeped in.
normal.cn: seepage 是表示渗进来的水的名词。

normal.en: Contrast leak: leak names the hole or the escape, seep names the slow flow.
normal.cn: 对比 leak：leak 强调漏洞或漏出，seep 强调缓慢的流动。

normal.en: Doubt seeped into their minds means the doubt arrived very slowly.
normal.cn: doubt seeped into their minds 表示疑虑来得很慢。

normal.en: The long vowel in seep makes the word feel as slow as the dripping it describes.
normal.cn: seep 的长元音让这个词听起来和它描述的滴漏一样慢。

abstract.en: Watch a drop race down a stone wall and then spread dark across the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水沿着石墙慢慢淌下，在墙上洇开一片深色。

abstract.en: Picture bad news entering a quiet room through a door left slightly open.
abstract.cn: 想象坏消息从一扇虚掩的门悄悄溜进安静的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a slow hour draining away while you wait.
abstract.cn: 想象你等待时，一个钟头静静地流走了。

examples.en: Cold air seeped into the old house through the gaps.
examples.cn: 冷空气从缝隙里渗进这座老房子。

examples.en: Rumours seeped through the village over the winter.
examples.cn: 谣言在整整一个冬天里慢慢传遍了村子。

examples.en: The soil was dark where the water had seeped up from the river.
examples.cn: 河水渗上来的地方，土壤颜色很深。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「细爬」——水贴着缝隙细细地爬过去，正是 seep 的渗透感；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为与方言动词 sipe 同源，表示「细流、慢慢淌」；确切源形存疑，最早书面记录约在十六世纪，核心义「细小而缓慢地流动」一直保留至今。

sensesIntro.en: Seep starts with a liquid flowing through tiny openings, then spreads to anything that creeps in slowly, and finally to the leaks and natural flows themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: seep 先指液体穿过细孔缓慢流动，再引申到任何慢慢侵入的事物，最后指渗漏现象与天然渗流本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of water spreading slowly through a crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴水沿着裂缝慢慢洇开。

branches.en: Liquid passing through tiny openings is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 液体穿过细孔流动是物理义项。

branches.en: Ideas spreading bit by bit borrow the liquid image.
branches.cn: 观念一点一点扩散，借用了液体的画面。

branches.en: Time and qualities that slip away slowly use the same slowness.
branches.cn: 时间与特征悄然流逝，用的是同一种慢。

branches.en: A leak is just the seep seen as an event or a place.
branches.cn: 渗漏就是把渗这个动作看成事件或地点。

branches.en: Natural oil seeps are the same process on a geological scale.
branches.cn: 天然石油渗出是同一过程在地质尺度上的版本。

intro.en: Seep is a short native verb; its small family grows with the suffixes -age, -ing, and -y.
intro.cn: seep 是一个简短的本族语动词，它的词族通过 -age、-ing、-y 等词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Seep is not from Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: seep 并非源自拉丁语，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: to trickle slowly through small openings
items.example: Water seeps through the sand.
items.exampleCN: 水透过沙子渗下。

items.example: The pipe seeps all winter.
items.exampleCN: 这根管子整个冬天都在渗水。

items.example: News seeped out slowly.
items.exampleCN: 消息慢慢传了出去。

items.example: A seeping damp smell filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 一股潮湿的霉味弥漫在房间里。

items.meaning: action or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示行为或行为结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -age turns seep into seepage.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 把 seep 变成 seepage。

items.meaning: a slow leak or liquid that has leaked
items.example: Engineers checked the dam for seepage.
items.exampleCN: 工程师检查大坝有无渗漏。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词与形容词的词尾
items.example: Seeping describes liquid that is leaking out.
items.exampleCN: seeping 形容正在渗出的液体。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the adjective seepy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成形容词 seepy。

items.example: A seepy cellar smells of wet stone.
items.exampleCN: 渗水的地窖里有湿石头的味道。

definition_zh: 地震仪；地震记录仪；地震计
definition_en: an instrument that records the strength and movement of earthquakes
core_image: 一个吊在半空的重摆，地面摇晃时笔尖在纸上画出密密麻麻的波线
scene: 实验室里，一台地震仪把远处发生的那次地震画成了一道道起伏的曲线。The seismograph in the laboratory turned a distant earthquake into a row of rising and falling lines.
sceneCN: 这里 seismograph 是「地震仪」（第 1 个义项：记录地震强弱与地面运动的仪器）；句意：实验室里，一台地震仪把远处发生的那次地震画成了一道道起伏的曲线。

pos.zh: （比喻）记录社会或情绪震动的记录器

derivatives.zh: 由 seismograph 加 -ic 构成，义为「地震仪（记录）的」
由 seismograph 加 -y 构成的名词，义为「地震记录、地震测量技术」
由希腊词根 seismo-（震动）加 -logy（学科）构成，义为「地震学」
由希腊词根 seism- 加 -ic 构成，义为「地震的；震动的」
由 seismo- 加 -gram（记录）构成，义为「地震波记录图」

senses.title: An instrument for recording earthquakes
senses.definition: a device that detects and draws a trace of the shaking of the ground
senses.definitionCN: 探测地面震动并把它画成轨迹的装置
senses.example: The seismograph recorded a small shock just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 地震仪在午夜刚过记录到一次轻微震动。
senses.why: Greek seismos means an earthquake, and graphu means I write, so the name literally says earthquake writer.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 seismos 意为地震，graphu 意为书写，合起来字面就是「写地震的工具」。

senses.title: The apparatus and its record taken together
senses.definition: the instrument and the visual record of movements it produces, often used loosely
senses.definitionCN: 仪器本身及其产生的运动记录，使用时常不加区分
senses.example: The seismograph showed sharp peaks at the exact time of the explosion.
senses.exampleCN: 地震仪在爆炸发生的确切时刻显示出尖锐的波峰。
senses.why: In ordinary use people point to the sheet of wavy lines and still call it a seismograph.
senses.whyCN: 日常使用中，人们指着那张波浪线记录，也照样叫它地震仪。

senses.title: Early pendulum or mechanical types
senses.definition: a heavy pendulum instrument in which a pen marks a moving drum
senses.definitionCN: 以重摆为原理、由笔尖在转动的记录鼓上留下痕迹的仪器
senses.example: Curators restored a pen seismograph from the eighteen nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 策展人修复了一台十九世纪九十年代的笔式地震仪。
senses.why: The first designs put a heavy weight and a pen together, and that image still defines the word for many people.
senses.whyCN: 最早的机型就是重锤加笔尖的组合，这个画面至今仍是许多人心中的释义。

senses.title: A network measurement device
senses.definition: a sensor within a station network that monitors ground motion continuously
senses.definitionCN: 台站网络中持续监测地面运动的传感器
senses.example: Each town now runs a seismograph linked to the regional centre.
senses.exampleCN: 现在每个城镇都装了一台与区域中心联网的地震仪。
senses.why: Modern instruments send digital readings day and night, so the word shifts from an object to a node in a watchful system.
senses.whyCN: 现代仪器昼夜不停地发送数字读数，这个词于是从一件物品转变成监测系统中的一个节点。

senses.title: A recorded trace of a shock
senses.definition: a visual trace of any strong shock, such as a blast or a tremor
senses.definitionCN: 任何强烈震动的可视痕迹，如爆炸或地震引起的抖动
senses.example: The rockfall left a sudden line across the seismograph.
senses.exampleCN: 岩崩在地震仪上留下了一道突发的线条。
senses.why: Because a seismograph answers to motion, not only to earthquakes, its trace can also read other shocks.
senses.whyCN: 地震仪只对振动做出反应而不限于地震，所以它的记录也能读出别种冲击。

senses.title: A figurative recorder of upheaval
senses.definition: a writer or work that records violent change in society, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指记录社会剧烈变化的作家或作品
senses.example: The novelist was called the seismograph of an uneasy age.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家被称为那个不安时代的「地震仪」。
senses.why: The instrument notices tiny tremors before the surface cracks, and critics borrow that image for sensitive observers.
senses.whyCN: 仪器能在表面开裂前察觉细微震动，批评家便借这个形象来形容敏感的观察者。

intro.en: Seismograph joins Greek seismos, an earthquake, with graphos, a writer or a writing.
intro.cn: seismograph 由希腊语 seismos（地震）与 graphos（书写者、书写）组合而成。

items.en: Seismos means a shaking or an earthquake, and graphos means a writer.
items.cn: seismos 意为震动或地震，graphos 意为书写者。

items.en: Scientific Latin builds compounds with these Greek parts from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，科学拉丁语用这两个希腊词根构造复合词。

items.en: The word appears as pendulum instruments begin to record ground motion.
items.cn: 随着摆式仪器开始记录地面运动，该词出现。

items.en: Seismograph becomes the usual name after a wave of large earthquakes.
items.cn: 经历一波大地震之后，seismograph 成为通用名称。

items.en: Seismograph and seismometer are often used side by side for the same equipment.
items.cn: 二十世纪起，seismograph 与 seismometer 常被并用于指同一种设备。

items.en: Digital networks keep the pen image alive while the recorded trace is now data.
items.cn: 数字台网保留了笔尖的画面，而记录痕迹今天已是数据。

note.en: Seismograph is the earthquake-writing compound; its near family includes the instrument, its subject, and its science.
note.cn: seismograph 是「写地震」的复合词，它的近邻包括仪器、研究对象与学科。

entries.definition: relating to a seismograph or its records
entries.definitionCN: 地震仪的；地震记录的

entries.definition: the written trace of ground motion
entries.definitionCN: 地震图；震动记录曲线

entries.definition: relating to the science of earthquakes
entries.definitionCN: 地震学的；与地震研究相关的

entries.definition: an instrument for detecting small ground movements
entries.definitionCN: 地震计；检测地面微小运动的仪器

entries.definition: the scientific study of earthquakes
entries.definitionCN: 地震学

entries.definition: an instrument that records strong ground acceleration
entries.definitionCN: 强震加速度记录仪

normalIntro.en: Seismograph says seismo and graph: an earthquake and a writing, joined into one word.
normalIntro.cn: seismograph 由 seismo 与 graph 两个部分合成：地震与书写，拼成一个词。

normal.en: Seismo in seismology and seismometer all means shaking of the earth.
normal.cn: seismology 与 seismometer 里的 seismo 都表示大地震动。

normal.en: Graph in biography and photograph means writing or drawing.
normal.cn: biography 与 photograph 里的 graph 都表示书写或描绘。

normal.en: A seismograph station names the fixed place where the instrument sits.
normal.cn: seismograph station 指仪器固定安放的地点。

normal.en: Contrast seismometer: a seismometer senses the motion, a seismograph writes it down.
normal.cn: 对比 seismometer： seismometer 感受震动， seismograph 把震动写下来。

normal.en: Seismology is the study, seismography is the recording craft.
normal.cn: seismology 是研究，seismography 是记录的技术。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy ball hanging still while the floor begins to shake.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沉重的摆球静静悬着，而地板开始抖动。

abstract.en: Watch a pen draw a jagged line in time with a passing lorry.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖随着一辆驶过的卡车画出一条锯齿线。

abstract.en: See the trace of an explosion strike the paper as one sharp spike.
abstract.cn: 想象爆炸的痕迹在纸上撞出一根尖锐的峰。

examples.en: The seismograph at the mountain station picked up the tremor immediately.
examples.cn: 山上观测站的地震仪立刻捕捉到了这次轻微震动。

examples.en: Engineers used seismographs to measure how the bridge moved in the wind.
examples.cn: 工程师用地震仪测量桥梁在风中的晃动。

examples.en: A century-old seismograph still traces the slow breathing of the hills.
examples.cn: 一台百年的地震仪仍在记录山丘缓慢的呼吸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞斯莫格拉夫」——可以想象一位叫「塞斯」的人拿着一支笔，把地震一笔一笔记下来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 seismos（震动、地震）+ graphos（书写者、书写）→ 科学拉丁语合成词 → 英语 seismograph，字面义「书写地震的器具」，核心义「把地面震动转成可读的痕迹」。

sensesIntro.en: Seismograph begins as the machine that writes earthquake motion, then covers the instrument with its record, early pendulum designs, networked sensors, other shock traces, and finally a figurative recorder of upheaval.
sensesIntro.cn: seismograph 先是记录地震运动的机器，继而涵盖仪器连同记录、早期摆式设计、台网传感器、其他冲击的痕迹，最后延伸到比喻意义上记录社会震动的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen drawing waves while the ground shakes.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面摇晃时，笔尖画出波浪线。

branches.en: The instrument itself is the central sense.
branches.cn: 仪器本身是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: Instrument and record blur together in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 日常说法里，仪器与记录常常混为一谈。

branches.en: Early pendulum designs give the word its classic picture.
branches.cn: 早期摆式设计赋予这个词经典的画面。

branches.en: Networked sensors and shock traces are the modern system sense.
branches.cn: 联网传感器与震动痕迹构成现代系统义项。

branches.en: A sensitive writer is called a seismograph for the same reason.
branches.cn: 敏感的作家被比作地震仪，道理相同。

intro.en: Seismograph is a Greek compound of seismo and graph, with science words built from the same two pieces.
intro.cn: seismograph 是 seismo 与 graph 构成的希腊语复合词，许多科学词都由这两块拼成。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, borrowed into Latin scientific writing as seismos and graphus.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个成分来自希腊语，以 seismos 与 graphus 的形式进入拉丁语科学文献。

items.example: Seismo- appears in seismology and seismometer.
items.exampleCN: seismo- 出现在 seismology 与 seismometer 中。

items.meaning: an instrument that writes or records
items.example: The suffix -graph forms telegraph and photograph.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -graph 构成 telegraph 与 photograph。

items.meaning: the art or process of writing
items.meaningCN: 书写或记录的技术与过程
items.example: The suffix -y forms seismography.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 seismography。

items.example: Seismology grew fast in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: 地震学在二十世纪迅速发展。

items.example: A seismometer is often paired with a recorder.
items.exampleCN: 地震计常与记录器配套使用。

items.meaning: the trace left by a seismograph
items.example: The seismogram showed two clear arrivals.
items.exampleCN: 地震图显示出两个清晰的到达波。

items.example: Seismographic records are now digital.
items.exampleCN: 地震记录如今已是数字化的。

items.example: The seismograph was bolted to bedrock.
items.exampleCN: 这台地震仪被固定在基岩上。

items.example: Seismographic data helped locate the fault.
items.exampleCN: 地震仪数据帮助确定了断层位置。

items.example: Modern seismography relies on digital sensors.
items.exampleCN: 现代地震记录依赖数字传感器。

definition_zh: 语义的；意义的；（计算机）语义的
definition_en: relating to meaning in language, or to the sense rather than the form of something
core_image: 同一个词像标签一样贴在两种物件上，读的人要辨出底下真正指什么
scene: 在阅读课上，老师引导学生区分一个词的字面意义和它在上下文里的语义差别。In the reading class, the teacher asked students to see the semantic difference between the literal sense of a word and its use in context.
sceneCN: 这里 semantic 是「语义的」（第 1 个义项：与词句意义相关的）；句意：在阅读课上，老师引导学生区分一个词的字面意义和它在上下文里的语义差别。

derivatives.zh: 由 semantic 加 -s 构成的名词，义为「语义学、意义」
由 semantic 加 -ally 构成，义为「在语义上、从意义上说」
由 semantic 加 -ist 构成，义为「语义学家」

senses.title: Relating to meaning in language
senses.definition: connected with the meaning of words and sentences rather than their sound or spelling
senses.definitionCN: 与词句的意义相关，而不是与读音或拼写相关
senses.example: The two words are close in sound but far apart in semantic range.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个词读音相近，语义范围却相差很远。
senses.why: The Greek root semainein means to show or to signify, so the adjective names whatever carries meaning.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 semainein 意为显示、指示，所以这个形容词指一切与传达意义有关的东西。

senses.title: Meaning as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 意义层面的；与形式相对的
senses.definition: concerning what something means instead of how it looks or sounds
senses.definitionCN: 关注某事物表示什么，而不是它看起来或听起来怎样
senses.example: The poem works through sound rather than semantic effect.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗靠声音而不是靠语义效果起作用。
senses.why: When form and meaning are set against each other, semantic marks the meaning side.
senses.whyCN: 当形式与意义被拿来对照时，semantic 专门标记「意义」这一侧。

senses.title: Technical use in engineering and computing
senses.definition: describing what symbols or code really mean to the system that processes them
senses.definitionCN: 描述符号或代码对处理它们的系统究竟意味着什么
senses.example: The team debated the semantic of the tag before shipping the update.
senses.exampleCN: 发布更新之前，团队争论了这个标签的语义。
senses.why: Computing takes the linguistic idea of meaning and applies it to data that is read by machines.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域把语言学中「意义」的概念搬到机器读取的数据上。

senses.title: A serious point instead of a quibble
senses.definition: making a point about substance rather than about words alone
senses.definitionCN: 关涉实质要点，而非仅纠缠字眼
senses.example: Much of the dispute was semantic, but the deadline was real.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争论多半是字面上的，但截止日期却是实实在在的。
senses.why: People separate a semantic quarrel from a real conflict, using the word to weigh words against facts.
senses.whyCN: 人们把「字面之争」与真正的冲突区分开，用这个词来衡量字眼与事实的分量。

senses.title: Study of meaning as a field
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of study that examines how meaning is organised
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究意义如何组织起来的学科分支
senses.example: She moved into semantic research after years of translation work.
senses.exampleCN: 做了多年翻译之后，她转向语义研究。
senses.why: As linguists developed semantics as a discipline, the adjective came to label the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把语义学建成一门学科之后，这个形容词也用来标记这一整个领域。

senses.title: Meaning carried by a label or code
senses.definition: the meaning that a label, marking, or symbol carries for those who read it
senses.definitionCN: 标签、标记或符号对阅读者所承载的含义
senses.example: The colours on the map have a semantic value of their own.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上的颜色本身就有一种语义价值。
senses.why: Anything read as a sign, not only a word, can be said to have semantic value.
senses.whyCN: 凡是被当作符号来读的东西，不只是词语，都可以说具有语义价值。

intro.en: Semantic comes from Greek semantikos, able to signify, from semainein, to show or to indicate.
intro.cn: semantic 来自希腊语 semantikos（能表示意义的），源于 semainein（显示、指示）。

items.en: Semainein means to show, to signal, or to signify.
items.cn: semainein 意为显示、发出信号或表示。

items.en: French linguists coin semantique for the study of meaning.
items.cn: 法国语言学家造出 semantique 一词，指对意义的研究。

items.en: English borrows the adjective as semantic, opening a new branch of language study.
items.cn: 英语借入形容词 semantic，开出一个语言研究的新分支。

items.en: Philologists write of semantic change and semantic fields.
items.cn: 语文学家开始谈论语义演变与语义场。

items.en: Computing borrows the term for the meaning of code and data.
items.cn: 二十世纪，计算机领域借这个词指代码与数据的意义。

items.en: A semantic issue now often means a dispute over words rather than facts.
items.cn: 今天说某问题是语义问题，往往意味着争的是字眼而非事实。

note.en: Semantic belongs to the Greek meaning family, beside semantics, semiotics, and ordinary words about sense.
note.cn: semantic 属于希腊语中表示「意义」的词族，与 semantics、semiotics 以及日常的「意义」类词相邻。

entries.definition: the study or the meaning of signs and words
entries.definitionCN: 语义学；意义

entries.definition: in terms of meaning
entries.definitionCN: 在语义上

entries.definition: the study of signs and symbols
entries.definitionCN: 符号学，与 semantic 共享希腊语词根，但侧重点不同

entries.definition: what a word or sign stands for
entries.definitionCN: 意义；含义

entries.definition: relating to language
entries.definitionCN: 语言的；语言学的

entries.definition: following the basic sense of words
entries.definitionCN: 字面上的；字面的

normalIntro.en: Semantic carries the Greek root for signifying, so it always points back to meaning.
normalIntro.cn: semantic 带着希腊语里「表示」的词根，总是指向意义。

normal.en: Semantics is the noun, so semantic change means a change in meaning.
normal.cn: semantics 是它的名词，所以 semantic change 指意义的变化。

normal.en: Semantically is the adverb, as in they are semantically related.
normal.cn: semantically 是副词，如说它们语义上相关。

normal.en: A semantic field groups words that share a meaning area.
normal.cn: semantic field 把共享一个意义领域的词归在一起。

normal.en: Contrast phonetic: phonetic is about sound, semantic is about sense.
normal.cn: 对比 phonetic：phonetic 关于声音，semantic 关于意义。

normal.en: Semantics and semiotics share the Greek idea of the sign.
normal.cn: semantics 与 semiotics 共享希腊语「符号」的概念。

abstract.en: Picture one label pasted on two very different objects.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张标签贴在两个截然不同的物件上。

abstract.en: Hear two words that sound alike but mean totally different things.
abstract.cn: 想象两个听起来相似、意思却完全不同的词。

abstract.en: Think of a computer tagging every line of code with a hidden meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象计算机给每一行代码都贴上一个隐藏的含义。

examples.en: The translation kept the logic but lost some semantic detail.
examples.cn: 这份译文保住了逻辑，却丢掉了部分语义细节。

examples.en: Linguists track semantic shifts across centuries of usage.
examples.cn: 语言学家追踪几百年用法中的语义变化。

examples.en: The editor noticed a semantic clash between the two sentences.
examples.cn: 编辑发现这两句话之间存在语义冲突。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思曼提克」——「思」考「曼」妙的意义，题（提）出语义；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 semainein（显示、指示，词干 sema- 意为符号）→ 希腊语形容词 semantikos → 法语 semantique → 英语 semantic / semantics，核心义「指向意义、承载意义」。

sensesIntro.en: Semantic begins with the meaning of words, widens to meaning as opposed to form, then to technical code meaning, to substantial points in argument, to the field of study, and to value carried by signs.
sensesIntro.cn: semantic 先指词句的意义，再扩展到与形式相对的意义、技术中的代码含义、争论里的实质要点、专门的研究领域，以及符号所承载的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same label pasted on two different things.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张标签贴在两种不同的物件上。

branches.en: Words and their meaning give the basic sense.
branches.cn: 词语及其意义构成基本义项。

branches.en: Meaning set against form is the contrastive sense.
branches.cn: 与形式相对的意义是对照义项。

branches.en: Machine-read code meaning is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 机器可读的代码含义是技术义项。

branches.en: Flags and sign values both judge what lies beneath the surface.
branches.cn: 旗帜与符号价值都在衡量表面之下的东西。

branches.en: The study of meaning grows directly from the word sense.
branches.cn: 对意义的研究直接由词义义项生长出来。

intro.en: Semantic is built on the Greek sign root sema with the suffix -ic, and its family grows beside semantics.
intro.cn: semantic 建立在希腊语「符号」词根 sema 加词尾 -ic 之上，它的词族与 semantics 一同生长。

latinIntro.en: The Greek root sema, a sign, reached Latin usage through Greek scientific writing.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语词根 sema（符号）经由希腊科学文献进入拉丁语用法。

items.example: Sema- underlies the word for the study of signs.
items.exampleCN: sema- 是「符号研究」一词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms semantic from the root.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 由词根构成 semantic。

items.example: Semantics names the study of meaning.
items.exampleCN: semantics 指对意义的研究。

items.meaningCN: 以……方式构成的副词词尾
items.example: Semantically means in terms of meaning.
items.exampleCN: semantically 表示在语义上。

items.meaning: a person who does or studies
items.meaningCN: 表示从事者或研究者的词尾
items.example: Who calls a semantist is rare today.
items.exampleCN: 如今很少用 semantist 称呼人。

items.example: Semiotics studies signs, semantics studies meaning.
items.exampleCN: 符号学研究符号，语义学研究意义。

items.example: Semantic change is common in every language.
items.exampleCN: 语义变化在每种语言里都很常见。

items.example: Semantics is often paired with syntax.
items.exampleCN: 语义学常与句法学并列讨论。

items.example: The two sentences are semantically identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两个句子在语义上完全相同。

definition_zh: 语义学；意义（尤指词语或陈述的意义）；（编程）语义
definition_en: the study of meaning in language, or the meaning that a word or statement actually carries
core_image: 一只手拿笔在词旁写下「这是什么意思」的注解
scene: 语法课上老师反复追问一个词到底指什么。Half the class argued about the semantics of the word fair.
sceneCN: 这里 semantics 指「语义学、对词义的学问」（第 1 个义项：研究语言意义的学科）；句意：半个班在争论 fair 这个词的语义。

derivatives.zh: 由 -ic 构成形容词，义为「语义的；意义方面的」
由 -ally 构成副词，义为「从语义上；在意义层面」
由 -ist 构成指人名词，义为「语义学家」
复合形容词，义为「不涉及语义的」

senses.title: The study of meaning in language
senses.definition: the branch of linguistics that studies the meaning of words, sentences and other language units
senses.definitionCN: 研究词、句子等语言单位意义的语言学分支
senses.example: She took a course in semantics and pragmatics.
senses.exampleCN: 她修了一门语义学与语用学课程。
senses.why: The Greek suffix -ics names a field of study, so the meaning root becomes the name of the science of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语后缀 -ics 表示「某门学科」，于是表示「意义」的词根就变成了研究意义的学问之名。

senses.title: The meaning carried by a word
senses.definition: the meaning that a particular word, phrase or statement actually carries
senses.definitionCN: 某个词语或说法实际承载的意义
senses.example: The semantics of the notice are unclear.
senses.exampleCN: 这份通知的语义并不清楚。
senses.why: By a short step, the science of meaning lends its name to the specific meaning of a particular expression.
senses.whyCN: 再走一小步，研究意义的学科之名就被借来指某个具体说法所携带的意义。

senses.title: Quibbling over wording
senses.titleCN: 咬文嚼字；斤斤计较于措辞
senses.definition: playful or dismissive use suggesting that a dispute is only about words and not about substance
senses.definitionCN: 玩笑或轻视的用法，暗示争论只是措辞之争而非实质分歧
senses.example: Call it a fee or a tax; that is just semantics.
senses.exampleCN: 叫它费用还是税，那不过是咬文嚼字。
senses.why: If a disagreement is only about meaning, people say it is just semantics, and the word itself becomes a label for word games.
senses.whyCN: 如果分歧只在意义层面，人们就说「不过是语义问题」；于是这个词本身成了「文字游戏」的代称。

senses.title: Meaning in programming
senses.definition: the agreed meaning of a program or of a piece of code, as opposed to its surface form
senses.definitionCN: 程序或代码片段约定的意义，相对于它表面的书写形式而言
senses.example: The compiler follows the semantics of the language standard.
senses.exampleCN: 编译器遵循语言标准的语义。
senses.why: Computer science borrows the linguistic idea: code has a written form and a separate meaning, and semantics is that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学借用了语言学概念：代码有书写形式和彼此独立的意义，而语义就是那个意义。

intro.en: Semantics comes from Greek semantikos, significant, from semainein, to mean or to signify, built on sema, a sign.
intro.cn: semantics 来自希腊语 semantikos（有意义的），源于 semainein（表示、示意），其根是 sema（符号、标记）。

items.en: Sema means a sign or mark that points to something.
items.cn: sema 意为指向某物的符号或标记。

items.en: Semainein means to signify or to show by a sign.
items.cn: semainein 意为示意、用符号表达。

items.en: Semantique is coined after the adjective semantique, concerning meaning.
items.cn: 十九世纪法语造出 semantique，由形容词 semantique（关于意义的）而来。

items.en: Semantics enters English as the name of the study of meaning, generally credited to the linguist Michel Breal.
items.cn: semantics 进入英语，作为「意义研究」的学科名，一般认为归功于语言学家布雷阿尔。

items.en: Logical and formal semantics develop, and computing borrows the word for the meaning of code.
items.cn: 逻辑语义学与形式语义学发展起来，计算机领域也借用该词表示代码的意义。

note.en: Semantics sits in the same family as semantic, semaphore and signal, all tracing back to the Greek sign, while its neighbours name meaning, usage and the smallest units of sound.
note.cn: semantics 与 semantic、semaphore、signal 同属「符号」一族，都能追溯到希腊语的「标记」；它的近邻则分别指意义、用法与最小的语音单位。

entries.definition: relating to meaning in language
entries.definitionCN: 语义的；与意义有关的

entries.definition: a system of signalling with flags or lights
entries.definitionCN: 旗语或灯语信号系统，与语义学同源于符号一词

entries.definition: a sign that carries information
entries.definitionCN: 传递信息的信号，与语义学共享「标记」这一古老词根

entries.definition: what a word or statement stands for
entries.definitionCN: 意义；意思

entries.definition: the study of how context shapes the use of language
entries.definitionCN: 研究语境如何影响语言使用的语用学

entries.definition: the study of the structure of words
entries.definitionCN: 研究词语结构的形态学

normalIntro.en: Semantics is the sign that means something: sema is a sign, and the -ics ending turns it into a field of study.
normalIntro.cn: semantics 就是会指向某物的「标记」：sema 是符号，后缀 -ics 把它变成一门学科。

normal.en: The root sema means a sign, so semantics is the study of what signs point to.
normal.cn: 词根 sema 意为符号，所以语义学就是研究符号指向什么。

normal.en: Like physics, it ends in -ics, which marks a science or a field.
normal.cn: 它和 physics 一样以 -ics 结尾，这个后缀标记一门科学或领域。

normal.en: Its adjective semantic drops the -s and means relating to meaning.
normal.cn: 它的形容词 semantic 去掉 -s，表示与意义有关。

normal.en: A semantic shift is a change in a word sense over time.
normal.cn: 语义演变指一个词的意义随时间发生改变。

normal.en: Speakers compare semantics with syntax: semantics is meaning, syntax is structure.
normal.cn: 讲者常把语义学与句法学对比：语义学管意义，句法学管结构。

abstract.en: Picture a committee sitting at a table, asking what does this word really mean.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会围桌而坐，追问这个词到底是什么意思。

abstract.en: Imagine a label stuck on a jar, reading its own contents back to you.
abstract.cn: 想象罐子上贴的标签，反过来向你读出罐里的东西。

abstract.en: Think of two people arguing over the same word while agreeing on the facts.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人为一个词争得面红耳赤，对事实却意见一致。

examples.en: Semantics is one of the core areas of modern linguistics.
examples.cn: 语义学是现代语言学的核心领域之一。

examples.en: The debate turned on the semantics of a single sentence.
examples.cn: 这场辩论的关键在于一个句子的语义。

examples.en: Do not get lost in semantics; tell me what actually happened.
examples.cn: 别在字面上较劲，直接告诉我到底发生了什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞满提及」——一个词被塞满各种提及它的意思，这就是语义研究；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 sema（符号、标记）→ semainein（示意、表示）→ semantikos（有意义的）→ 法语 semantique → 英语 semantics，核心义「标记所指之义」。

sensesIntro.en: Semantics starts as the science of meaning, then names the meaning of a single expression, then its everyday dismissal as mere wordplay, and finally the meaning of code.
sensesIntro.cn: semantics 先指研究意义的学科，再指单个说法的意义，随后被日常用来轻视措辞之争，最后指代码的意义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand writes the question what does this mean beside a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在单词旁边写下「这是什么意思」。

branches.en: The field of study is the primary sense and the one that names the discipline.
branches.cn: 学科义是首要义项，也是给这门学问命名的义项。

branches.en: The meaning of a single word is the borrowing of the science name for its object.
branches.cn: 单词的意义是借学科名来指该学科研究的对象。

branches.en: The dismissive wordplay sense grows from disputes that concern only meaning.
branches.cn: 轻视性的咬文嚼字义，由只关乎意义的争论生长而来。

branches.en: The computing sense transfers meaning from signs to code.
branches.cn: 计算机义把「意义」从语言符号转移到代码上。

branches.en: Naming the meaning of a word and studying meaning share one object: what an expression means.
branches.cn: 为单词命名意义与研究意义共有同一对象：某个说法意味着什么。

intro.en: Semantics is built on the Greek root sem, sign, plus the study ending -ics, and it supports semantic, semantically and semanticist.
intro.cn: semantics 由希腊词根 sem（符号）加学科后缀 -ics 构成，并衍生出 semantic、semantically 与 semanticist。

latinIntro.en: No Latin family is needed here: the word goes back through French to Greek sema, a sign, and its relatives are the Greek sem and sign words.
latinIntro.cn: 这里无需依赖拉丁同族：该词经法语追溯到希腊语 sema（符号），同族词属于希腊表示符号和标记的词群。

items.example: The root sem- names a mark that stands for something.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sem- 指代表某物的标记。

items.example: Sema is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: sema 是最早有记录的词形。

items.example: Semainein is the verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: semainein 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms semantic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 semantic。

items.example: Semantic describes meaning rather than form.
items.exampleCN: semantic 描述的是意义而非形式。

items.example: The suffix -ics turns an adjective into a science name.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ics 把形容词变成学科名。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms semantically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ally 构成 semantically。

items.example: Semantically stresses the meaning side of a contrast.
items.exampleCN: semantically 强调对比中的意义一面。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms semanticist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 semanticist。

items.example: A semanticist studies how meanings are carried.
items.exampleCN: 语义学家研究意义是如何被承载的。

definition_zh: 年资；资历；资深地位；年长
definition_en: the rank or advantage that a person gains from having worked or served longer than others
core_image: 队伍按加入时间的先后排开，站得最前的人资历最深
scene: 公司新来的年轻人发现，加薪顺序只看谁先入职。Promotion here depends on seniority rather than talent.
sceneCN: 这里 seniority 指「资历、年资」（第 1 个义项：因任职或服务时间更长而获得的地位与优势）；句意：这里的升职取决于资历而非才能。

derivatives.zh: seniority 的基础形容词，义为「年长的；资深的；级别较高的」
由形容词转作名词，义为「年长者；资深者；上级」
由 -ly 构成副词，义为「在资历或级别上更靠前地」

senses.title: Length of service as a rank
senses.definition: the rank or advantage that comes from having served longer than other people in a job or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 因在职位或组织中任职时间比他人更长而获得的等级或优势
senses.example: Promotion depends on seniority rather than talent.
senses.exampleCN: 升职取决于资历而非才能。
senses.why: Latin senior means older, and -ity turns it into the abstract quality of being older in service, so years become rank.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 senior 意为「较年长的」，后缀 -ity 把它变成抽象性质，即任职更久的状态，于是年数变成了等级。

senses.title: Being older in age
senses.definition: the state of being older than another person, often used in formal or legal contexts
senses.definitionCN: 比他人年长的状态，多用于正式或法律语境
senses.example: The rule prefers the child of greater seniority.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则优先照顾年长的孩子。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simple age, and this sense survives in formal writing beside the workplace sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层意思就是年龄，这一义项在正式文体中与职场义并存。

senses.title: Precedence given by long service
senses.definition: a special claim or right, such as choosing shifts or avoiding a layoff, that long service earns
senses.definitionCN: 因长期任职而得到的特殊权利要求，如优先挑选班次或免于被裁员
senses.example: Her seniority gave her first pick of the shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 她的资历让她第一个挑选班次。
senses.why: Once length of service is ranked, it turns into a claim: those with more of it are treated first.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任职时间被排成等级，它就变成一种权利要求：资历越多的人越先被优待。

senses.title: The senior people as a group
senses.titleCN: 资深者的地位；在长辈或上级中的位置
senses.definition: the standing of someone as the older or more senior member of a family, body or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 作为家庭、机构或会议中年长者或级别较高者的地位
senses.example: He spoke with the seniority of the eldest brother.
senses.exampleCN: 他以长兄的资深地位发言。
senses.why: The quality can be attached to a person and mark how far up the order of age or rank that person stands.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质可以附着在个人身上，标示此人在年龄或等级序列中站得多靠前。

intro.en: Seniority is Latin senior, older, the comparative of senex, old, plus the noun suffix -ity.
intro.cn: seniority 由拉丁语 senior（较年长的，senex「老」的比较级）加名词后缀 -ity 构成。

items.en: Senex means old, and its stem sen- gives the family its base.
items.cn: senex 意为年老，其词干 sen- 构成这个词族的基础。

items.en: Senior means older, as a comparative form of senex.
items.cn: senior 是 senex 的比较级，意为较年长的。

items.en: Senator names an elder, literally an old man, showing how age became office.
items.cn: senator 字面意为「老人」，显示年长如何转化为公职身份。

items.en: Seignor, a lord, carries the senior notion of authority into French.
items.cn: 古法语 seignor（领主）把 senior 所带的权威意味带入法语。

items.en: Seniority appears as a noun naming the state of being older or higher in rank.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 seniority 作为名词出现，指年长或等级较高的状态。

items.en: Industrial and union rules turn seniority into a formal workplace right.
items.cn: 现代工业与工会规则把 seniority 变为职场中的正式权利。

note.en: Seniority belongs to the Latin family of senex, old, beside senior, senator and senile, and it stands near rank, precedence and tenure.
note.cn: seniority 属于拉丁语 senex（老）词族，与 senior、senator、senile 同源；它在意义上与等级、优先权与任职期相接近。

entries.definition: older or higher in rank
entries.definitionCN: 年长的；资深的；级别较高的

entries.definition: a member of a senate, originally an elder
entries.definitionCN: 参议员，原义为元老，与 seniority 同源于「老」

entries.definition: showing the weakness of old age
entries.definitionCN: 年迈衰弱的，同样来自表示「老」的词根

entries.definition: a position in a scale of importance
entries.definitionCN: 等级；级别

entries.definition: the right to go or be treated before others
entries.definitionCN: 优先权；居先

entries.definition: the period during which a post is held
entries.definitionCN: 任期；任职期

normalIntro.en: Seniority is built from senior, the Latin word for older, plus the state ending -ity: it is the state of being the older or longer-serving one.
normalIntro.cn: seniority 由 senior（拉丁语「较年长的」）加状态后缀 -ity 构成：它就是「更年长、任职更久」的状态。

normal.en: The base word senior means older, and -ity turns it into a quality.
normal.cn: 基础词 senior 意为较年长的，-ity 把它变成一种性质。

normal.en: Like majority and authority, it names a state, not a person.
normal.cn: 它和 majority、authority 类似，指一种状态而非某个人。

normal.en: Years of seniority are counted from the day a person joined.
normal.cn: 资历年限从入职那一天开始计算。

normal.en: A seniority system promotes workers in order of their start dates.
normal.cn: 资历制度按员工入职先后顺序晋升。

normal.en: Compare senior, the person or post, with seniority, the standing.
normal.cn: 对比 senior（人或职位）与 seniority（所处的地位）。

abstract.en: Picture a queue ordered by the date on each badge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队伍，按每人证件上的日期排定先后。

abstract.en: Imagine a wall of birthday cards, oldest at the left.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙的生日卡，最年长的排在左边。

abstract.en: Think of a job board where short service gets the last choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一块排班板，工龄最短的人最后挑选。

examples.en: In many unions, layoffs are decided strictly by seniority.
examples.cn: 在许多工会里，裁员完全按资历决定。

examples.en: She has fifteen years of seniority in the department.
examples.cn: 她在该部门已有十五年资历。

examples.en: Younger staff often complain that seniority counts more than results.
examples.cn: 年轻员工常抱怨资历比业绩更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「先入理」——先入职的人有道理、有地位，因为资历深；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 senex（年老）→ senior（较年长的）→ 中古英语 senior → 加 -ity 构成 seniority，核心义「因年长或任职更久而被排在前面的地位」。

sensesIntro.en: Seniority first means rank earned by length of service, then simple older age, then the privileges that long service brings, then the standing of a senior person within a group.
sensesIntro.cn: seniority 先指由任职时长换来的等级，再指单纯的年长，然后指长年服务带来的特权，最后指个人在群体中作为长者的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: people line up by the date on their badges, oldest at the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：人们按证件上的日期排队，资历最深的站在最前。

branches.en: Rank by length of service is the main workplace sense.
branches.cn: 按任职时长的等级是主要的职场义项。

branches.en: Simple older age is the oldest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 单纯的年长是这个词最古老的一层意思。

branches.en: The rights of long service turn rank into advantage.
branches.cn: 长期任职的权利把等级变成了实际好处。

branches.en: The standing of a senior member applies the quality to a person.
branches.cn: 资深成员的地位把这种性质落实到具体的人身上。

branches.en: Rank and precedence both rest on the same count of years.
branches.cn: 等级与优先权都建立在对同一年数的计算之上。

intro.en: Seniority is the adjective senior, older, plus the noun suffix -ity, and its family includes senior, senator and senile.
intro.cn: seniority 是形容词 senior（年长的）加名词后缀 -ity，同族词包括 senior、senator 与 senile。

latinIntro.en: Latin senex, old, gives the comparative senior and the office word senator; -ity is the Latin -itas that names a quality or state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 senex（老）给出比较级 senior 与官职词 senator；后缀 -ity 源自拉丁语 -itas，表示性质或状态。

items.example: The root sen- carries the idea of age.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sen- 承载「年长」的概念。

items.example: Senex is the source word of the family.
items.exampleCN: senex 是这个词族的源词。

items.example: Senior is the comparative of senex.
items.exampleCN: senior 是 senex 的比较级。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ity turns senior into seniority.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把 senior 变成 seniority。

items.example: Senior staff sit at the front.
items.exampleCN: 资深员工坐在前排。

items.example: The senior approves the schedule.
items.exampleCN: 资历最深者批准排班表。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms seniorly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 seniorly。

items.example: Seniorly is rare but well formed.
items.exampleCN: seniorly 虽罕见但构词正确。

items.example: Senator shows age turning into office.
items.exampleCN: senator 显示年长如何转化为公职。

items.example: Senile keeps the plain old-age sense.
items.exampleCN: senile 保留了单纯的年老义。

definition_zh: 轰动的；耸人听闻的；引起强烈兴趣的；极好的
definition_en: causing great excitement or strong public interest, often in a way that exaggerates; also used informally to mean excellent
core_image: 报纸头版被一行巨大的黑体标题撑满，路人纷纷抬头
scene: 小报把一则普通车祸写成了惊天大案。The tabloid ran a sensational story about the crash.
sceneCN: 这里 sensational 是「耸人听闻的、渲染性的」（第 1 个义项：以夸张方式引发强烈公众兴趣的）；句意：这份小报刊登了一篇关于那场车祸的耸人听闻的报道。

pos.zh: 轰动的；耸人听闻的；极好的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，由 -ion 构成，义为「感觉；轰动的事件」
由 -ism 构成，义为「煽情主义；耸人听闻的报道风格」
由 -ize 构成动词，义为「把……渲染成轰动新闻」
由 -ist 构成，义为「惯于耸人听闻的人或报刊」
由否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不煽情的；平实的」

senses.title: Causing strong public excitement
senses.definition: arousing great public interest or excitement, often by presenting events in an exaggerated way
senses.definitionCN: 引起强烈公众兴趣或激动，常以夸张方式呈现事件
senses.example: The paper printed a sensational account of the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸刊登了对该案审理的耸人听闻的报道。
senses.why: The base noun sensation first meant a physical feeling, then a rush of excitement, and the adjective marks whatever stirs it.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词 sensation 先指身体感觉，再指一阵激动，形容词便指能引发这种激动的东西。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: used informally to praise something as wonderfully good or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，称赞某事物极好或令人印象深刻
senses.example: Her first novel is a sensational read.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说读起来精彩绝伦。
senses.why: When the excitement becomes positive, the same word slides into simple hearty praise.
senses.whyCN: 当激动的情绪转为正面，同一个词就滑入淳朴的赞美，表示好得令人兴奋。

senses.title: Relating to physical sensation
senses.definition: technical or rare use relating to sensation, the feeling of the body or the senses
senses.definitionCN: 技术或罕见用法，与感觉相关，即身体或感官的知觉
senses.example: The skin has a sensational nerve network.
senses.exampleCN: 皮肤有一套感觉神经网络。
senses.why: The oldest layer of sensation is bodily feeling, and the adjective keeps this literal sense in older medical and philosophical writing.
senses.whyCN: sensation 最古老的一层是身体感觉，形容词在旧的医学与哲学文本里保留了这一字面义。

senses.title: Remarkable enough to be remembered
senses.definition: remarkably striking in a way that stands out from the ordinary and stays in memory, often said of results or events
senses.definitionCN: 因格外突出而被人记住的，常用来形容成果或事件
senses.example: The team made a sensational start to the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队以惊人的开局开始了本赛季。
senses.why: Anything that produces a sensation is noticed and remembered, so the word also marks striking achievements without any suggestion of exaggeration.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能引起轰动的都会被注意并记住，因此这个词也用来标记突出的成就，并不带夸张意味。

intro.en: Sensational is sensation plus the adjective suffix -al; the root goes back to Latin sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: sensational 由名词 sensation 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，其词根可追溯到拉丁语 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire means to feel, to perceive, and also to think.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、知觉，也指思考。

items.en: Sensus is the noun of feeling and understanding.
items.cn: sensus 是表感觉与理解的名词。

items.en: Sensatio means a perception through the senses.
items.cn: sensatio 意为经由感官所得到的感觉。

items.en: The noun sensation is used for bodily feeling and perception.
items.cn: 名词 sensation 在英语中指身体感觉与知觉。

items.en: Sensation widens to mean a striking event and a stir of excitement, giving sensational its dramatic meaning.
items.cn: sensation 扩展为「轰动事件」与「轰动」，由此产生了 sensational 的戏剧化含义。

items.en: Journalists and advertisers make sensational a standard word of praise and blame.
items.cn: 记者与广告商让 sensational 成为常用词，既可褒也可贬。

note.en: Sensational is the adjective of sensation, close to sensual, sensitive and senseless in spelling, and near dramatic, striking and lurid in meaning.
note.cn: sensational 是 sensation 的形容词，拼写上与 sensual、sensitive、senseless 相近；意义上与戏剧化的、惊人的、耸动低俗的诸词相邻。

entries.definition: a feeling or a stir of excitement
entries.definitionCN: 感觉；轰动

entries.definition: relating to bodily pleasures
entries.definitionCN: 肉体的；感官享受的，虽同源于感觉，但只涉及身体快感

entries.definition: quick to feel or react
entries.definitionCN: 敏感的；易受影响的

entries.definition: sudden and striking
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧性的；引人注目的

entries.definition: grabbing attention by being unusual
entries.definitionCN: 引人注目的；突出的

entries.definition: shocking and told in a tasteless, greedy way
entries.definitionCN: 耸动而低俗地渲染的

normalIntro.en: Sensational is sensation plus -al: it describes whatever makes a sensation, a jolt of excitement that everyone notices.
normalIntro.cn: sensational 是 sensation 加后缀 -al：它描述能制造轰动、惊动所有人的东西。

normal.en: Sensation comes from Latin sentire, to feel, so a sensation is something felt.
normal.cn: sensation 来自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），所以 sensation 是被感觉到的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -al means relating to, so sensational means relating to a sensation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 意为「与……有关的」，所以 sensational 意为与感觉、轰动有关。

normal.en: The -ize form sensationalize means to turn news into a sensation.
normal.cn: 加 -ize 构成的 sensationalize 意为把新闻炒作成轰动事件。

normal.en: The -ism form sensationalism names the style of chasing thrills.
normal.cn: 加 -ism 构成的 sensationalism 指追逐刺激的报道风格。

normal.en: Keep it apart from sensitive, which means easily hurt or easily moved.
normal.cn: 注意与 sensitive 区分，后者意为敏感的、易受伤的。

abstract.en: Picture a huge front page headline shouting one word.
abstract.cn: 想象头版上一行巨大的标题只喊出一个词。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd turning its head at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在同一瞬间齐刷刷转过头。

abstract.en: Think of a newspaper page printed in ink that looks too bold.
abstract.cn: 想象一页报纸，墨色浓得过分刺眼。

examples.en: The press focused on the most sensational details of the case.
examples.cn: 媒体专挑这件案子最耸人听闻的细节来报道。

examples.en: She has made a sensational start to her singing career.
examples.cn: 她的演唱生涯一开始就引起了轰动。

examples.en: The novel is loud and sensational rather than thoughtful.
examples.cn: 这部小说喧闹煽情，而不是发人深省。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「心事深」（sense 加 -ational）——心里事情太多就制造轰动，想得「深」的人最爱夸张；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sentire（感觉）→ sensatio（感觉）→ 英语 sensation（感觉；轰动）→ 加 -al 构成 sensational，核心义「能制造强烈感觉与轰动」。

sensesIntro.en: Sensational first means causing a public sensation, usually through exaggeration, then extreme praise, then the literal sense of bodily sensation, and finally anything striking enough to be remembered.
sensesIntro.cn: sensational 先指引发公众轰动，通常经由夸张；再指极高的赞美；然后是身体感觉的字面义；最后指任何足以被记住的突出事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newspaper front page filled by one huge headline.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整版报纸被一行巨大的标题占满。

branches.en: Causing a public stir is the main sense and the usual target of criticism.
branches.cn: 引发公众轰动是主要义项，也常是批评的对象。

branches.en: Extreme praise is the positive drift of the same excitement.
branches.cn: 极高赞美是同一激动情绪的正面走向。

branches.en: The bodily sensation sense is the oldest literal layer.
branches.cn: 身体感觉义是最古老的字面层次。

branches.en: Anything remarkable that creates a sensation is remembered as striking.
branches.cn: 凡造成轰动而被记住的事物，都可用作「惊人」。

branches.en: Both the exaggerated story and the remarkable result draw attention sharply.
branches.cn: 夸张的报道与出色的成果都以锐利的方式抓住注意力。

intro.en: Sensational is sensation plus -al, with sensation built from Latin sens, feel, plus -ation, and the family includes sensitive, sensual and sensible.
intro.cn: sensational 是 sensation 加后缀 -al，而 sensation 由拉丁词根 sens（感觉）加 -ation 构成，同族词还有 sensitive、sensual 与 sensible。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire, to feel, gives sensus, sensatio and the English sensation; the suffixes -ation and -al sit on this root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire（感觉）给出 sensus、sensatio 与英语 sensation；后缀 -ation 与 -al 都建立在这个词根上。

items.example: The root sens- means to feel.
items.exampleCN: 词根 sens- 意为感觉。

items.example: Sentire is the deepest source of the family.
items.exampleCN: sentire 是这个词族最深的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ation forms sensation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 sensation。

items.example: Sensation carries both the body and the crowd.
items.exampleCN: sensation 同时承载身体与人群两层意义。

items.example: The suffix -al forms sensational.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 sensational。

items.meaningCN: 表示做法或主义的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism forms sensationalism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 sensationalism。

items.meaning: the habit of chasing thrills in the news
items.meaningCN: 煽情主义；耸人听闻的报道方式
items.example: Sensationalism sells papers.
items.exampleCN: 煽情报道能让报纸畅销。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms sensationalize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 sensationalize。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms sensationalist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 sensationalist。

items.example: The suffix -tive forms sensitive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tive 构成 sensitive。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms sensible.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 sensible。

definition_zh: 感官的；诉诸感官的；给人感官享受的；细腻悦人的
definition_en: appealing to the senses rather than the mind, and giving pleasure through touch, sound, colour or taste
core_image: 指尖抚过丝绸，触感顺着皮肤一圈圈荡开
scene: 清晨的布料店里，她闭上眼用手指慢慢划过一叠绸缎。The sensuous touch of the silk made her forget the noise of the street.
sceneCN: 这里 sensuous 是「感官上的、给人感官享受的」（第 1 个义项：与感官或感官愉悦有关）；句意为丝绸那种细腻的触感让她忘了街上的喧闹。图中可辨识物件：绸缎、手指、布店木柜。

pos.zh: 感官的；诉诸感官的；给人感官享受的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「感官地；给人以感官享受地」
基础词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「感官性；感官享受的特质」
由 sense 一系加后缀 -ality 构成，多指肉体情欲；与 sensuous 同源，但意味更重
同一个 sense 词根加后缀 -ory 构成，义为「感觉的、感官的」，偏科学用法
否定前缀 in- 加基础词构成，义为「不诉诸感官的」，现已偏罕用

senses.title: Relating to the senses
senses.definition: connected with the senses rather than with the reasoning mind
senses.definitionCN: 与感官有关，而不是与理性思考有关
senses.example: He thinks in images and colours, always after sensuous detail.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠图像和色彩来思考，总是追求感官上的细节。
senses.why: The Latin root sentire means to feel, and sensuous keeps that felt, bodily channel rather than the thinking one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 sentire 是「感觉」，sensuous 紧紧抓住的是「被感觉到」这一渠道，而不是「被想到」的渠道。

senses.title: Pleasing to the senses
senses.definition: attractive and giving pleasure to touch, taste, sound, smell or sight
senses.definitionCN: 在触、味、听、嗅、视上悦人，带来愉悦
senses.example: The garden offered a sensuous mix of warm stone and jasmine.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里温暖的石头与茉莉香气交织，令人沉醉。
senses.why: If a thing is felt through the senses, it can also be felt as delightful, so the word slides from perception to pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 既然是靠感官去感受的东西，就能被感受为令人愉悦的东西，于是词义从「感知」滑向「享受」。

senses.title: Rich in texture or sound
senses.titleCN: 细腻悦人的；优美动人的
senses.definition: describing music, language or texture that is rich, smooth and deeply felt
senses.definitionCN: 形容音乐、语言或质感丰厚、柔润、触动人心
senses.example: The cellist drew out a long, sensuous note.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴手拉出一个绵长而柔润的音。
senses.why: The pleasure sense narrows onto art: sound and surface become the most noticeable carriers of sensuous feeling.
senses.whyCN: 「享受」这一义继续聚焦到艺术上：声音与表面成了最能承载感官感受的载体。

senses.title: Distinguished from sensual
senses.definition: used for aesthetic pleasure in contrast with sensual, which carries a sexual or indulgent tone
senses.definitionCN: 用于审美愉悦，与带有情欲或放纵意味的 sensual 形成对照
senses.example: Critics praise the poem as sensuous rather than sensual.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这首诗是「感官悦人」而非「情欲的」。
senses.why: It arose in the seventeenth century as a near twin with a cleaner edge, so the word itself now marks the line between beauty and appetite.
senses.whyCN: 它在十七世纪与 sensual 几乎成双出现，却多了一层干净的意味，于是这个词本身就标记了「美感」与「欲望」之间的界线。

senses.title: Vivid, concrete description
senses.definition: describing writing that appeals to the senses by naming colours, sounds and textures
senses.definitionCN: 形容写作通过颜色、声音、质感的描写来打动感官
senses.example: Her prose is sensuous: every page smells of rain and bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文字很有感官感：每一页都带着雨和面包的气味。
senses.why: Writing that reaches the senses works on the same channel as the body, so critics call such description sensuous.
senses.whyCN: 能触及感官的文字与身体走的是同一条通道，于是评论家把这种描写称为 sensuous。

intro.en: Sensuous comes from Latin sentire, to feel, through the derived adjective sensuosus, and was formed in English as a more delicate twin of sensual.
intro.cn: sensuous 源自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），经由派生形容词 sensuosus；它在英语中成形，是 sensual 一件更雅致的双胞胎。

items.en: Sentire means to feel, perceive or notice through the senses.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、感知、通过感官察觉。

items.en: Sensuosus, full of feeling, is commonly derived from the noun sensus, a sense or perception.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 sensuosus 意为「充满感觉的」，一般认为由名词 sensus（感觉、知觉）派生。

items.en: Sensuous appears in English, with the first attestation given as 1640 in standard dictionaries.
items.cn: sensuous 在英语中首次出现，通行词典给出的首见年份为 1640 年。

items.en: Poets such as Milton used it as a refined alternative to sensual, to mean pleasing to the senses.
items.cn: 弥尔顿等诗人把它当作 sensual 的雅化替代，表示「悦人感官的」。

items.en: Modern English extends it to art, music and prose with rich sensory texture.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到具有丰富感官质感的艺术、音乐与文章。

note.en: Sensuous sits close to sensual, sensible and the sense word family, and near beauty words such as voluptuous and lush.
note.cn: sensuous 与 sensual、sensible 以及 sense 词族关系密切，意义上也邻近 voluptuous、lush 这类「丰润悦人」的词。

entries.definition: relating to the body and sexual pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 肉体的；情欲的，与 sensuous 同源，但更强调身体与欲望

entries.definition: reasonable and wise in practical matters
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；通情达理的，与 sensuous 同出 sentire 词根

entries.definition: of the sense organs or the process of sensing
entries.definitionCN: 感官的；感觉的，多用于科学语境

entries.definition: without meaning or without consciousness
entries.definitionCN: 无意义的；失去知觉的

entries.definition: giving pleasure to the senses, especially in a full and rich way
entries.definitionCN: 丰润诱人的；给人强烈感官享受的

entries.definition: rich, thick and pleasing to the senses
entries.definitionCN: 茂盛的；丰润悦人的

entries.definition: concerned with beauty and the appreciation of beauty
entries.definitionCN: 审美的；美感的

normalIntro.en: Sensuous keeps the sense root but adds a soft u, and that soft sound is a good handle for the gentle, aesthetic side of pleasure.
normalIntro.cn: sensuous 保留 sense 词根，却多出一个柔和的 u 音，这个柔和的读音正好能用来记住它温和、审美的那一面。

normal.en: Sense is the root: sensuous things can be touched, heard or tasted.
normal.cn: 词根是 sense：sensuous 的东西是能被摸到、听到、尝到的。

normal.en: Compare sensible, which keeps the mind, while sensuous keeps the body.
normal.cn: 对比 sensible：sensible 留着头脑，sensuous 留着身体。

normal.en: Sensual carries a sexual edge, sensuous stays with beauty.
normal.cn: sensual 带情欲色彩，sensuous 停留在美感上。

normal.en: Critics call writing with colour and smell sensuous prose.
normal.cn: 评论家把充满颜色与气味的文字称为 sensuous prose。

normal.en: Sensuous pleasure is the pleasure of silk, honey and a warm cello note.
normal.cn: sensuous pleasure 是丝绸、蜂蜜与温暖大提琴音带来的愉悦。

abstract.en: Picture fingertips moving over a bolt of silk, feeling the grain without asking what it costs.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖划过一匹绸缎，只感受它的纹理，而不问价钱。

abstract.en: Imagine a painter who does not describe the fruit but makes you taste it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家不描述水果，却让你尝到它的味道。

abstract.en: Think of the difference between a sensible plan and the warm touch of the hand that carries it out.
abstract.cn: 想一想一个明智的计划与执行它的那只温暖的手之间的区别。

examples.en: The designer chose sensuous fabrics, silk and velvet, for the winter collection.
examples.cn: 设计师为冬季系列挑选了丝绸和天鹅绒这类柔润的布料。

examples.en: Her voice had a sensuous quality that held the whole audience.
examples.cn: 她的嗓音有一种悦耳的质感，抓住了全场观众。

examples.en: Critics describe the novel as sensuous rather than sensual.
examples.cn: 评论家把这部小说形容为感官悦人，而非情欲的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森苏丝」——森林里的苏打水滑过丝绸：触感细腻、悦人感官；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sentire（感觉、感知）→ sensus（感官、知觉）→ 晚期拉丁语 sensuosus（充满感觉的）→ 英语 sensuous（悦人感官的）；核心义「经身体感受而生的愉悦」。

sensesIntro.en: Sensuous starts as relating to the senses, becomes pleasing to them, narrows to rich texture in art, and finally earns its own identity next to sensual.
sensesIntro.cn: sensuous 从「与感官有关」出发，转为「悦人感官」，再聚焦到艺术中丰润的质感，最后在与 sensual 的区分中确立了自己的身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingertips moving slowly across a bolt of silk.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖缓缓划过一匹绸缎。

branches.en: The basic sense names the channel of the senses themselves.
branches.cn: 基础义项命名的正是「感官」这条通道本身。

branches.en: Once the channel carries delight, the word means pleasing to the senses.
branches.cn: 一旦这条通道承载了愉悦，这个词就表示「悦人感官」。

branches.en: Art makes texture and colour the sharpest carriers, so music and prose are called sensuous.
branches.cn: 艺术让质感与色彩成为最鲜明的载体，于是音乐与文章被称为 sensuous。

branches.en: The word also marks a boundary, keeping beauty apart from appetite.
branches.cn: 这个词还划出一条边界，把美感与欲望分开。

branches.en: A sensuous description and a sensuous fabric work the same way: both make you feel rather than explain.
branches.cn: 感官化的描写与悦人的布料运作方式相同：都让你去感受，而不是解释。

intro.en: Sensuous belongs to the sentire family, alongside sense, sensible, sensuousness and sensory.
intro.cn: sensuous 属于 sentire 词族，与 sense、sensible、sensuousness、sensory 同出一源。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire means to feel, and its noun sensus gives us sense, sensation and sensuosus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 意为感觉，其名词 sensus 衍生出 sense、sensation 与 sensuosus。

items.example: Sentire supplies the feeling root.
items.exampleCN: sentire 提供「感觉」这一词根。

items.example: Sensus is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Sensuosus is the direct base of the English word.
items.exampleCN: sensuosus 是英语词的直接基础。

items.example: The suffix -ous turns sensus into sensuous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把 sensus 变成 sensuous。

items.example: Sense is the plain family member.
items.exampleCN: sense 是词族里最朴素的一员。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sensuously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 sensuously。

items.example: Sensuousness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: sensuousness 指这种性质。

items.example: Sensory is the scientific sibling.
items.exampleCN: sensory 是科学语境里的兄弟词。

items.example: The prefix in- forms insensuous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 insensuous。

definition_zh: 有感觉的；有知觉的；有意识的；能感知的
definition_en: able to feel and be aware of things, especially of pleasure and pain
core_image: 指尖碰到滚烫的杯子，整只手立刻缩回来
scene: 实验室里，志愿者把手轻轻放在加热板上，碰到的瞬间就缩了回去。Even a tiny insect is sentient enough to avoid the flame.
sceneCN: 这里 sentient 是「有感觉、有知觉的」（第 1 个义项：能感受疼痛和快乐）；句意为连一只小昆虫都足够有知觉，会躲开火焰。图中可辨识物件：加热板、实验手套、观察窗。

pos.zh: 有感觉的；有知觉的；有意识的

collocations.zh: 有情众生；有知觉的生命

derivatives.zh: 基础词去尾加 -ce 构成，义为「知觉；意识；感受力」，是这一组里最常用的名词
同义名词变体，后缀为 -cy，与 sentience 通用但较少见
否定前缀 in- 加基础词构成，义为「无感觉的、无知觉的」
基础词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「带有知觉地、有意识地」

senses.title: Able to feel
senses.definition: able to feel things physically, especially pleasure and pain
senses.definitionCN: 能在身体上感受到东西，尤其是快乐与疼痛
senses.example: The debate asks whether fish are sentient and can suffer.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争论在问鱼是否具有感觉、是否会受苦。
senses.why: The Latin present participle sentiens means feeling, so the adjective names a creature that is actually feeling at this moment.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语现在分词 sentiens 意为「正在感觉的」，所以这个形容词命名的是此刻真的在感受着的生命。

senses.title: Conscious and aware
senses.definition: having conscious awareness of oneself and the surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 对自身与周围环境有意识觉察
senses.example: Scientists still argue about what makes a system sentient.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家们仍在争论是什么让一个系统具有意识。
senses.why: Feeling deepens into knowing that one feels, and that self-awareness is what the word now guards most carefully.
senses.whyCN: 「感觉」进一步深化为「知道自己正在感觉」，而这种自我觉察正是这个词如今最看重的含义。

senses.title: A sentient being
senses.titleCN: 有情众生；有知觉的生命
senses.definition: a living creature that can experience things, used especially in ethics and religion
senses.definitionCN: 能够体验事物的生命体，多用于伦理与宗教语境
senses.example: Buddhist teaching urges care for all sentient beings.
senses.exampleCN: 佛教教义劝人关怀一切有情众生。
senses.why: The adjective is often turned into a noun for moral purposes: whoever can suffer deserves consideration.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常被名词化，用于道德讨论：凡是能受苦的生命都值得被考虑。

senses.title: Sentient machines
senses.definition: describing a machine or program said to have feelings or awareness
senses.definitionCN: 形容被说成有感受或意识的机器、程序
senses.example: No current computer is genuinely sentient.
senses.exampleCN: 目前没有任何计算机是真正有意识的。
senses.why: Modern English pushes the word past biology, asking whether a mind could one day be built rather than born.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把这个词推离生物学，追问心灵是否可能被制造出来，而不只是被生出来。
