senses.title: Sensitive in older use
senses.definition: a literary or older sense meaning responsive to impressions and feelings
senses.definitionCN: 文学或用旧的义项，指对印象和情感反应灵敏
senses.example: The Victorian poet described a sentient soul awake to every breeze.
senses.exampleCN: 那位维多利亚时代的诗人描写了一个对每一缕微风都敏感的魂灵。
senses.why: Before it settled on awareness, the word could simply mean quick to feel, close to sensitive.
senses.whyCN: 在固定为「有意识」之前，这个词可以只表示「感受敏捷」，与 sensitive 很接近。

intro.en: Sentient is the English form of the Latin present participle sentiens, feeling, from sentire, to feel, and it enters English through seventeenth-century scientific prose.
intro.cn: sentient 是拉丁语现在分词 sentiens（感觉着的）的英语形式，源自 sentire（感觉），十七世纪通过科学文章进入英语。

items.en: Sentire means to feel, perceive or be aware of something.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、感知、觉察到某物。

items.en: Sentiens, the present participle, means feeling or perceiving, as an action still going on.
items.cn: 现在分词 sentiens 意为「正在感觉、正在感知」，强调动作仍在持续。

items.en: The English adjective is first recorded in the early seventeenth century, with 1604 often given as the first attestation.
items.cn: 这个英语形容词最早见于十七世纪初，常以 1604 年作为首见年份。

items.en: Early scientific writers used it for things that can feel, in contrast with bodies that cannot.
items.cn: 早期的科学作者用它形容能感受之物，与不能感受的物体相对。

items.en: Modern English uses it in animal welfare, ethics and artificial intelligence.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于动物福利、伦理与人工智能。

note.en: Sentient shares its root with sentence, sentiment and sensible, and stands near conscious, aware and the Latin-based sapient.
note.cn: sentient 与 sentence、sentiment、sensible 同根，意义上邻近 conscious、aware，以及同样来自拉丁语的 sapient。

entries.definition: a feeling or opinion
entries.definitionCN: 情感；看法，与 sentient 同出 sentire

entries.definition: a grammatically complete unit of words
entries.definitionCN: 句子，原义为「想法」，与 sentient 同根

entries.definition: wise, showing deep knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 智慧的，只是拼写与 sentient 相近，词源不同，来自 sapere

entries.definition: showing tender feelings, often too easily
entries.definitionCN: 多愁善感的；易动情的，由 sentiment 派生

entries.definition: awake and aware of oneself and the surroundings
entries.definitionCN: 清醒的；有意识的

entries.definition: knowing that something exists or is happening
entries.definitionCN: 意识到的；知道的

entries.definition: living, not dead
entries.definitionCN: 活着的，sentient 比它多一层「能感受」

normalIntro.en: Sentient is built on sentire, the same root as sense and sentiment, with the participle ending -ient marking a state that is still going on.
normalIntro.cn: sentient 建立在 sentire 之上，与 sense、sentiment 同根，分词词尾 -ient 标记一种仍在持续的状态。

normal.en: Sentire is to feel, so sentient means currently feeling.
normal.cn: sentire 是「感觉」，因此 sentient 表示「此刻正在感受着」。

normal.en: The ending -ient marks the one who feels, as in patient and agent.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ient 标记「感受者」，就像 patient 和 agent 里的用法。

normal.en: Animal welfare law asks whether a creature is sentient.
normal.cn: 动物福利法会先问一种生物是否 sentient。

normal.en: Insentient reverses it: a stone is insentient.
normal.cn: insentient 是它的反面：石头就是 insentient 的。

normal.en: Compare sentiment, which is the feeling itself, while sentient is the one who feels.
normal.cn: 对比 sentiment：它是感觉本身，而 sentient 是感觉的那个主体。

abstract.en: Picture a hand jerking back from a hot cup before the mind has said a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在头脑来得及说话之前就缩离了滚烫的杯子。

abstract.en: Imagine standing in a dark room and knowing, without seeing, that someone else is there.
abstract.cn: 想象站在黑屋子里，看不见却知道旁边还有别人。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp and a moth: the lamp has no inside, the moth is sentient, it feels the heat.
abstract.cn: 想一想灯和蛾子：灯没有内在，蛾子却是 sentient 的，它感觉到热度。

examples.en: Many people now accept that insects are sentient to some degree.
examples.cn: 如今许多人承认昆虫在某种程度上是有感觉的。

examples.en: Ethicists ask whether a sentient machine would deserve rights.
examples.cn: 伦理学家在问一台有意识的机器是否应当享有权利。

examples.en: The treaty protects every sentient being from unnecessary suffering.
examples.cn: 这项条约保护每一个有情众生免受不必要的痛苦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森提恩特」——森林里提着一盏灯，忽然感到一阵凉：有感觉、有知觉；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sentire（感觉）→ 现在分词 sentiens / sentient-（正在感觉着的）→ 英语 sentient（有知觉的）；核心义「能感受、能觉察」。

sensesIntro.en: Sentient moves from the plain ability to feel, to self-aware consciousness, to the creatures and machines that are said to hold it, and to the older sense of being easily moved.
sensesIntro.cn: sentient 从「能够感受」出发，走到「自我觉察的意识」，再由被称作有知觉的生命与机器承载，最后保留「易受触动」这一旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand drawing back from a hot cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从滚烫的杯子前缩回。

branches.en: The base sense is simply the capacity to feel pain and pleasure.
branches.cn: 基础义项就是感受痛与乐的能力。

branches.en: Awareness adds a second layer: the creature knows that it feels.
branches.cn: 意识加上第二层：生命知道自己正在感受。

branches.en: Ethics turns the adjective into a noun for every creature that can suffer.
branches.cn: 伦理学把形容词名词化，指每一个能受苦的生命。

branches.en: Technology borrows the word to ask whether a mind could be made.
branches.cn: 技术领域借用这个词，追问心灵是否可以被制造出来。

branches.en: Being quick to feel and being able to feel are two degrees of the same root.
branches.cn: 「易于感受」与「能够感受」是同一词根的两个程度。

intro.en: Sentient belongs to the sentire family, together with sense, sentence, sentiment, sensitive and insentient.
intro.cn: sentient 属于 sentire 词族，与 sense、sentence、sentiment、sensitive、insentient 同出一源。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire means to feel, and its participle sentiens gives sentient and its noun sentientia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 意为感觉，其分词 sentiens 派生出 sentient 及其名词 sentientia。

items.example: Sentire supplies the feeling root.
items.exampleCN: sentire 提供「感觉」这一词根。

items.example: Sentiens is the form the English word copies.
items.exampleCN: sentiens 是英语词直接照搬的形式。

items.example: The ending -ent turns the feeling into sentient.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 把「感觉」变成 sentient。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms sentience.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成 sentience。

items.example: Sense is the plain family member.
items.exampleCN: sense 是词族里最朴素的一员。

items.example: Sentiment names the feeling itself.
items.exampleCN: sentiment 指感觉本身。

items.example: Sensitive is the easily moved sibling.
items.exampleCN: sensitive 是「容易被打动」的兄弟词。

items.example: The prefix in- forms insentient.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 insentient。

items.example: Insentient describes stones and desks.
items.exampleCN: insentient 描述石头和课桌。

definition_zh: 多愁善感的；感情用事的；感伤的；怀旧动人的
definition_en: showing or causing tender feelings, often about the past, and sometimes more than the situation deserves
core_image: 旧铁盒里的车票和照片被一张张摊开，眼睛渐渐湿了
scene: 搬家那天，她把旧铁盒里的车票和照片一张张摊在桌上，迟迟不肯收进行李。The sentimental value of the broken watch outweighed its price.
sceneCN: 这里 sentimental 是「多愁善感的、因旧物而动情的」（第 1 个义项：对过去的事物怀有柔软感情）；句意为这只坏掉的手表所承载的情感价值远超过它的价钱。图中可辨识物件：旧铁盒、车票、手表。

pos.zh: 多愁善感的；感情用事的；（事物）令人感伤怀旧的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「感情地；多愁善感地」
基础词加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「感伤主义；滥情作风」
基础词加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「多愁善感；感伤情调」
基础词去尾构成，义为「情感；看法」，是 sentimental 的直接来源
前缀 over- 加基础词构成，义为「过分感伤的、太煽情的」

senses.title: Tender feelings about the past
senses.definition: showing gentle, affectionate feelings, especially about old times or old objects
senses.definitionCN: 表现出温柔、眷恋的情感，尤其针对旧时光或旧物
senses.example: Seeing her first school brought back sentimental memories of childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 看到她的第一所学校，勾起了童年的怀旧记忆。
senses.why: The base sentiment means a feeling, and adding -al makes it a property of a person or occasion soaked in feeling.
senses.whyCN: 词干 sentiment 意为「情感」，加上词尾 -al 就变成「被情感浸透的人或场合」所带有的性质。

senses.title: Too much feeling, too little judgement
senses.titleCN: 感情用事的；动辄动情的
senses.definition: allowing feelings rather than reason to guide judgement or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 让情感而不是理性来主导判断或行为
senses.example: They kept the old car for purely sentimental reasons.
senses.exampleCN: 他们留下那辆旧车完全出于感情上的原因。
senses.why: Since feeling can override judgement, the word takes on a critical shade: sentimental people decide with the heart alone.
senses.whyCN: 既然情感能压过判断，这个词就带上了批评的色彩：多愁善感的人只凭心做决定。

senses.title: Designed to tug the heart
senses.definition: describing films, songs or writing that play on tender feelings in an exaggerated way
senses.definitionCN: 形容电影、歌曲或文字刻意夸张地撩动柔软的情绪
senses.example: The ending is sentimental and predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结尾煽情而老套。
senses.why: Anything built to move people can be judged by how hard it tries, so the word becomes a label for art that pulls tears on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 凡是意在打动人的东西都能按其用力程度受评判，于是这个词成了「刻意催泪的艺术」的标签。

senses.title: An object with emotional worth
senses.definition: describing an object or place valued for the feelings it carries rather than its price
senses.definitionCN: 形容因其承载的情感而非价格而受珍视的物品或地点
senses.example: The ring has sentimental value far beyond its price.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚戒指的情感价值远远超过它的价格。
senses.why: When feeling attaches to a thing, the word shifts from the person to the possession and marks its emotional worth.
senses.whyCN: 当情感附着在物品上，这个词就从人转移到物，标出它的情感价值。

senses.title: Sensitive in older use
senses.definition: an older literary sense meaning quick to feel emotion
senses.definitionCN: 文学中用旧的义项，指情感反应敏锐
senses.example: In her letters she was tender and sentimental, quick to tears.
senses.exampleCN: 在她的书信里，她温柔而感性，很容易落泪。
senses.why: The eighteenth-century word first meant simply marked by feeling, with none of the later criticism.
senses.whyCN: 这个十八世纪的词最初只表示「带有情感的」，并没有后来的贬义。

intro.en: Sentimental is built in English from sentiment, which comes from Latin sentire, to feel, with the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: sentimental 是在英语中由 sentiment 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，而 sentiment 来自拉丁语 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire means to feel, perceive or notice.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、感知、察觉。

items.en: Sentimentum, a feeling or opinion, arises in later Latin.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中出现 sentimentum，意为感觉或意见。

items.en: Sentement means a feeling, and passes into English as sentiment.
items.cn: 古法语 sentement 意为感觉，进入英语后成为 sentiment。

items.en: Sentimental is formed in the eighteenth century from sentiment and the suffix -al.
items.cn: sentimental 于十八世纪由 sentiment 加词尾 -al 构成。

items.en: By the late eighteenth century it gains the critical sense of excessive feeling.
items.cn: 到十八世纪末，它获得了「情感过度」的批评性含义。

items.en: Modern English uses it for both tender attachment and overdone emotion in art.
items.cn: 现代英语用它兼指温柔的依恋与艺术中过度的煽情。

note.en: Sentimental is the adjective of sentiment, with its family sentience, sensibility and sentimentalism, and it sits near nostalgic, emotional and romantic.
note.cn: sentimental 是 sentiment 的形容词形式，词族里有 sentience、sensibility、sentimentalism，意义上邻近 nostalgic、emotional、romantic。

entries.definition: a feeling or opinion held towards something
entries.definitionCN: 情感；看法，是 sentimental 的直接词基

entries.definition: able to feel and perceive
entries.definitionCN: 有知觉的，与 sentimental 同出 sentire

entries.definition: based on reason rather than feeling
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；理性的，与 sentimental 几乎相反

entries.definition: a feeling or a means of perceiving
entries.definitionCN: 感觉；感官，是整个词族的根

entries.definition: feeling happy and sad at the same time about the past
entries.definitionCN: 怀旧的；对往事又喜又悲的

entries.definition: having or showing strong feelings
entries.definitionCN: 情绪化的；被情绪左右的

entries.definition: too sentimental and therefore unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 过度感伤而令人反感的

normalIntro.en: Sentimental carries sentiment inside it, so the word looks like feeling turned into a habit of the heart.
normalIntro.cn: sentimental 里就带着 sentiment（情感），这个词看起来就是「把情感变成了一种习惯」。

normal.en: Sentiment is the noun, sentimental is the adjective of feeling.
normal.cn: sentiment 是名词，sentimental 是表示情感性质的形容词。

normal.en: The suffix -al makes the quality, so sentimental means full of sentiment.
normal.cn: 词尾 -al 表示性质，所以 sentimental 意为「充满情感的」。

normal.en: Sentimental value is the worth a thing has because of memories.
normal.cn: sentimental value 是一件东西因回忆而具有的价值。

normal.en: Send a sentimental message, not a sensible one, when you want to touch a heart.
normal.cn: 想打动人心时，寄一封 sentimental 的信，而不是 sensible 的信。

normal.en: The suffix -ity turns it into sentimentality, the habit of being sentimental.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ity 使它变成 sentimentality，也就是多愁善感的习性。

abstract.en: Picture an old tin box opened on a table, filled with tickets and faded photographs.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上打开一只旧铁盒，里面全是车票和褪色的照片。

abstract.en: Imagine a film that keeps playing soft piano music just before the hero cries.
abstract.cn: 想象一部总在主角落泪前放起轻柔钢琴曲的电影。

abstract.en: Think of a leaf pressed inside a book, worth nothing and worth everything at once.
abstract.cn: 想一想夹在书里的一片叶子：一文不值，又无价可估。

examples.en: She is not sentimental about the house and sold it without regret.
examples.cn: 她对这所房子并不感伤，毫无遗憾地把它卖掉了。

examples.en: They took a sentimental journey back to their old school.
examples.cn: 他们回到母校，做了一次怀旧之旅。

examples.en: The sentimental ending of the film divided the critics.
examples.cn: 影片煽情的结局让评论家们意见不一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森提门头」——站在森林的老门头前想起往事，眼泪就下来了：多愁善感、怀旧；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sentire（感觉）→ sentimentum（感觉、意见）→ 古法语 sentement → 英语 sentiment（情感）+ 后缀 -al → sentimental（感情的、感伤的）；核心义「被情感包裹」。

sensesIntro.en: Sentimental begins as the plain quality of feeling, turns toward tender attachment to the past, gains a critical edge for excess feeling, labels hearts-and-flowers art, and finally names the emotional worth of things.
sensesIntro.cn: sentimental 从「有情感的」这一朴素性质出发，转向对过去的温柔依恋，再带上「情感过度」的批评意味，成为煽情艺术品类的标签，最后用来指物品的情感价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old tin box of tickets and photographs opened on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上打开一只装着车票和照片的旧铁盒。

branches.en: The main sense keeps the warmth of sentiment for old times.
branches.cn: 主要义项保留了对旧时光的那份温情。

branches.en: When feeling guides choices, the word criticises poor judgement.
branches.cn: 当情感主导选择时，这个词就在批评判断失误。

branches.en: Art that forces tears is judged as sentimental rather than moving.
branches.cn: 硬要催泪的艺术便被判为 sentimental 而非动人。

branches.en: A thing with sentimental value borrows its worth from memory.
branches.cn: 有 sentimental value 的东西向回忆借来了价值。

branches.en: The older gentle sense is the root of the later criticism of too much feeling.
branches.cn: 早期温和的含义是后来批评「情感过度」的根源。

intro.en: Sentimental is sentiment plus the adjective suffix -al, and its family includes sentimentality, sentimentalism and the base sentiment.
intro.cn: sentimental 是 sentiment 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，词族包括 sentimentality、sentimentalism 及词基 sentiment。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire means to feel, giving sentimentum in later Latin and, through French, the English sentiment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 意为感觉，晚期拉丁语派生出 sentimentum，再经法语进入英语成为 sentiment。

items.example: Sentire lies under the whole family.
items.exampleCN: sentire 是整个词族的底层。

items.example: Sentimentum is the noun sentire produced.
items.exampleCN: sentimentum 是 sentire 产生的名词。

items.example: Sentiment is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: sentiment 是这个形容词的词基。

items.example: The suffix -al forms sentimental.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 sentimental。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sentimentally.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 sentimentally。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms sentimentality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sentimentality。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms sentimentalism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 sentimentalism。

items.example: The prefix over- forms oversentimental.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 oversentimental。

items.example: Sensible keeps the mind where sentimental keeps the heart.
items.exampleCN: sensible 守着头脑，sentimental 守着心。

definition_zh: 红杉；巨杉；北美红杉属的巨树；巨杉的木材；以巨杉命名的地名与保护区
definition_en: a very tall evergreen tree of the redwood family, native to the western United States, or the reddish timber of such a tree
core_image: 树干粗得能开进一辆马车、树顶直插云端的巨杉
scene: 游客站在巨杉脚下仰头，帽子都掉了下来。At the foot of a sequoia, the visitors tilted back their heads so far that some of them lost their hats.
sceneCN: 这里 sequoia 是「巨杉」（第 1 个义项：北美西部的高大针叶巨树）；句意：在巨杉脚下，游客们把头仰得很高，有人的帽子都掉了。

pos.zh: 红杉；巨杉；北美红杉属的巨树
巨杉木材；巨杉林；以巨杉命名的地方

collocations.zh: 巨杉（胸径巨大、树皮厚实的巨型红杉）

derivatives.zh: 由属名 Sequoia 复合希腊词 dendron（树）而得的属名，指巨杉
由 sequoia 加形容词后缀 -oid 构成，意为「类似红杉的」
复合词，指巨杉的球果，体积比枝干小得多

senses.title: The giant evergreen tree itself
senses.definition: an extremely tall evergreen conifer of the western United States, especially the giant sequoia and the coast redwood
senses.definitionCN: 美国西部极其高大的常绿针叶树，尤指巨杉与海岸红杉
senses.example: The largest sequoia in the park is taller than a cathedral.
senses.exampleCN: 公园里最大的那棵巨杉比一座大教堂还高。
senses.why: The name was given to a tree genus, so its first and most common sense is simply the living tree that bears the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字本来就是给一个树木属取的，所以最基本的义项就是「叫这个名字的活树」。

senses.title: The reddish timber of the tree
senses.definition: the reddish, soft and durable wood sawn from these trees, used for shingles, fences and furniture
senses.definitionCN: 从这类树上锯下的偏红、轻软且耐用的木材，用于木瓦、栅栏与家具
senses.example: The deck is built from sequoia that has lasted fifty winters.
senses.exampleCN: 这座木平台用的是红杉木，已经挨过了五十个冬天。
senses.why: Once the tree is felled, the name transfers by metonymy to the material, because timber is spoken of by the species it came from.
senses.whyCN: 树被伐倒后，名字就顺着「以物代树」的途径转指木材，因为木材总是按原树种来称呼。

senses.title: A stand or forest of these trees
senses.definition: a grove or forest in which such trees grow, often protected as a national park or monument
senses.definitionCN: 生长这类巨树的树丛或森林，常被划为国家公园或保护区加以保护
senses.example: We walked the sequoia in silence, our voices swallowed by the trunks.
senses.exampleCN: 我们默默穿行在巨杉林里，声音都被粗大的树干吞没了。
senses.why: In American usage a grove is often named after its dominant tree, so the species name can stand for the whole stand.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语常用林子的主要树种作为林地名，于是树种名可以代指整片林子。

senses.title: A place named after the tree
senses.definition: part of the name of national parks, valleys and streets in California, taken directly from the tree
senses.definitionCN: 加利福尼亚州国家公园、山谷和街道名称中的一部分，直接取自这种树
senses.example: They drove north from the valley to the sequoia park gates.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从山谷一路向北，开到巨杉公园的大门口。
senses.why: Proper names are coined by shifting a common noun into a place label, so the tree name becomes a map label.
senses.whyCN: 专有地名常由普通名词转用而来，于是树名变成了地图上的地名。

senses.title: The genus name in botanical Latin
senses.definition: the scientific genus name given to a group of huge conifers, written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 赋予一大类巨型针叶树的科学属名，书写时首字母大写
senses.example: Botanists still debate whether the sequoia should be split into two genera.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家至今仍在争论是否应把红杉属拆成两个属。
senses.why: Modern botany turned the common tree word into a formal genus label, and the capital letter marks the technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 现代植物学把这个普通的树名变成了正式的属名标签，首字母大写正是技术义项的标志。

senses.title: A symbol of immense age and size
senses.definition: a figurative image of something ancient, immense and calmly enduring
senses.definitionCN: 比喻某一古老、巨大而沉稳长久之物的意象
senses.example: His reputation is a sequoia that nothing in the storm can bend.
senses.exampleCN: 他的名声就像一棵巨杉，风暴里什么也折不断它。
senses.why: The sheer scale and age of the tree invite metaphorical transfer to anything that dwarfs those around it.
senses.whyCN: 树的高大与长寿极易被隐喻挪用到任何远超周围之物上，于是产生了象征义。

senses.title: A figure in the climate story
senses.titleCN: 碳汇与森林保护的象征
senses.definition: a shorthand in conservation and climate writing for a forest whose old, huge trees store enormous amounts of carbon
senses.definitionCN: 在环保与气候写作中泛指由古老巨树组成、储存极多碳的森林
senses.example: Protecting a single sequoia forest can lock away carbon for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 保护一片红杉林，就能把碳锁定好几个世纪。
senses.why: Because the trees live for thousands of years, conservation writing uses the name as a compact emblem of long-term carbon storage.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种树能活上千年，环保写作就用它的名字来简洁地象征长期的碳储存。

senses.title: The California tree letter initial
senses.definition: a loose informal use in which people apply the word to any very large red-barked conifer of the far west
senses.definitionCN: 一种宽泛的非正式用法，泛指美国远西部任何树皮偏红的大型针叶树
senses.example: The roadside sign simply said sequoia, though the tree was a Douglas fir.
senses.exampleCN: 路边牌子只写了「红杉」，尽管那棵树其实是花旗松。
senses.why: Popular labels generalise quickly, so a single famous species name gets stretched to cover look-alike roadside giants.
senses.whyCN: 通俗叫法扩散得很快，一个著名树种的名字就会被拉伸，去覆盖路边那些长得像的巨树。

intro.en: Sequoia is a modern botanical coinage, first printed in 1847 as a genus name for the Californian redwoods; the tree was named after the Cherokee scholar Sequoyah, and no Latin root is involved.
intro.cn: sequoia 是现代植物学新造的词，于十九世纪中叶首次以属名形式印出，取自幼年在美国长大的切罗基文字发明者塞阔雅之名，并非来自任何拉丁词根。

items.en: The name ultimately honors Sequoyah, the Cherokee scholar who invented the Cherokee syllabary.
items.cn: 这个名字最终是为了纪念塞阔雅，也就是发明了切罗基音节文字的切罗基学者。

items.en: In a common account the botanist Endlicher recalled the Cherokee name for the Oconee River, though this detail is uncertain.
items.cn: 一种常见说法是植物学家恩德利希回忆起了奥科尼河的切罗基语名称；不过这个细节来源不确定。

items.en: The name was printed as a genus label for the California redwoods.
items.cn: 这个名称当年作为属名标签，用来指称加州的红杉。

items.en: English travellers turned the Latin genus label into an ordinary, uncapitalised noun.
items.cn: 英语旅行者把这个拉丁属名变成了普通的小写名词。

items.en: The word spread with the national parks and today names parklands, streets and conservation campaigns.
items.cn: 随着国家公园的建立，这个词广泛流传，如今还被用来给园区、街道与环保运动命名。

note.en: Sequoia is a name-like botanical coinage, close to other giant conifers and to the places that carry the same name.
note.cn: sequoia 是一种近乎人名的新造植物名，与其它巨型针叶树以及同名地点相邻。

entries.definition: a very tall conifer with reddish wood
entries.definitionCN: 木材偏红、极其高大的针叶树，是 sequoia 的普通名词同义词。

entries.definition: more than one of these huge trees
entries.definitionCN: sequoia 的复数形式，指多棵巨杉。

entries.definition: the loss of a sound at the end of a word
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自希腊语，指词尾音脱落。

entries.definition: the family of tall red-barked Californian trees
entries.definitionCN: 加州那类树皮偏红的巨树，统称红杉。

entries.definition: a tall deciduous conifer of the same plant family
entries.definitionCN: 同科的高大落叶针叶树，常与红杉一并讨论。

entries.definition: a long-lived hardwood tree used as a symbol of strength
entries.definitionCN: 长寿的硬木树，同样常被用来象征力量与稳固。

normalIntro.en: Sequoia is a proper name turned tree name: remember the scholar Sequoyah, and the tree that outgrew him in fame.
normalIntro.cn: sequoia 是人名转成的树名：记住学者塞阔雅，还有那棵名声超出他的巨树。

normal.en: Giant sequoia is the species with the thickest bark and the heaviest trunk.
normal.cn: giant sequoia 指树皮最厚、树干最重的那种巨杉。

normal.en: A grove of sequoias is a stand of these trees, often protected as a monument.
normal.cn: a grove of sequoias 指一片巨杉林，常被列为保护区。

normal.en: Sequoia timber is reddish, light and resistant to rot, so it is used for shingles.
normal.cn: 巨杉木材偏红、轻软又耐腐，所以常被用来做木瓦。

normal.en: The plural is regular: one sequoia, two sequoias.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化：一株 sequoia，两株 sequoias。

normal.en: In scientific writing the genus name Sequoia keeps a capital letter.
normal.cn: 在科学写作中，属名 Sequoia 保留首字母大写。

abstract.en: Picture yourself standing at the root, your whole body smaller than one ring of bark.
abstract.cn: 想象你站在树根边，整个身子还比不上一圈树皮。

abstract.en: Imagine a plank table with visible red grain, sanded smooth by fifty winters.
abstract.cn: 想象一张红纹理清晰的木板桌，被五十个冬天磨得光滑发亮。

abstract.en: Stretch a thin rope around the trunk: it takes two people and several minutes to meet again.
abstract.cn: 想象用细绳把树干绕一圈：要好几个人接力，才能让绳子重新碰上起点。

examples.en: The sequoia in front of us was still growing after three thousand years.
examples.cn: 我们面前的那棵巨杉，三千多年后仍在生长。

examples.en: Rangers close part of the sequoia trail each winter to protect the roots.
examples.cn: 每年冬天，护林员会封闭红杉步道的一部分，以保护树根。

examples.en: Shingles made of sequoia are light and seldom rot.
examples.cn: 用红杉木做的木瓦又轻又不容易烂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛阔无涯」——一棵树宽得赛得过一个操场，高得望不到边；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 并非拉丁词根，而是近代植物学以切罗基学者塞阔雅之名新造的属名，首见印出一般都定在十九世纪中叶；树名借人名而成。

sensesIntro.en: Sequoia starts as the living tree, then passes to its timber, its groves, the places named after it, and finally to metaphor and conservation shorthand.
sensesIntro.cn: sequoia 先指活着的巨树，再转指其木材、树林与同名地点，最后引申为比喻与环保符号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single trunk so wide that a person seems tiny at its root.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株宽到让人站在根边显得极小的巨树树干。

branches.en: The living tree is the literal core of the word.
branches.cn: 活着的树是这个词最字面的核心义。

branches.en: The familiar label gets stretched over other giant conifers on roadsides.
branches.cn: 熟悉的树名沿路被拉宽，覆盖了其它巨树。

branches.en: Cutting the tree yields reddish timber named by species.
branches.cn: 把树伐下，就得到以树种命名的偏红木材。

branches.en: Groves, map labels and botanical genera all borrow the tree name.
branches.cn: 林地名、地图地名与植物属名都借用了这个树名。

branches.en: Scale and age make it a metaphor for endurance and stored carbon.
branches.cn: 体量与树龄使它成为持久与碳储存的隐喻。

intro.en: Sequoia has no English affixes; it is a proper name turned into a genus label, and English compounds such as giant sequoia do most of the work.
intro.cn: sequoia 本身没有英语词缀，它是人名转成的属名标签；英语里主要靠 giant sequoia 这类复合词来细分。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only the grammatical machinery of botanical names, such as the -a ending and the genus capital, not the word itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了植物学命名的语法框架，例如词尾与属名首字母大写，并没有提供这个词本身。

items.meaning: the genus of huge Californian redwoods
items.example: Sequoia is printed with a capital letter.
items.exampleCN: 属名 Sequoia 首字母大写。

items.meaning: a feminine noun ending common in plant names
items.meaningCN: 植物属名中常见的阴性名词词尾
items.example: The ending -a makes the name look like a Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -a 让这个名称看上去像拉丁名词。

items.example: Giant narrows the name to the heaviest species.
items.exampleCN: giant 把名称缩小到树干最重的那一种。

items.example: Redwood is the everyday synonym of the tree.
items.exampleCN: redwood 是这种树的日常同义词。

items.meaning: small woods or groups of trees
items.example: Groves often form part of park names.
items.exampleCN: 树丛常出现在公园名称里。

items.meaning: the outer covering of a tree trunk
items.example: Sequoia bark can be a foot thick.
items.exampleCN: 巨杉的树皮可以有一英尺厚。

items.meaning: the seed case of a conifer
items.example: The sequoia cone is small, the tree is not.
items.exampleCN: 巨杉的球果很小，树却不然。

items.example: Dendron combines to form the genus name Sequoiadendron.
items.exampleCN: dendron 组合成属名 Sequoiadendron。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms sequoioid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成 sequoioid。

definition_zh: 宁静的；安详的；晴朗的；温和的；平静的海；宁静晴朗的天空；崇高的称号
definition_en: calm and untroubled, clear of cloud or disturbance, or used in titles of honour to mean high and gracious
core_image: 雨停后的湖面，没有一丝风，天空也很干净
scene: 吵了一天之后，院子忽然安静下来，风也停了。After a noisy afternoon, the garden turned serene and the children spoke in whispers.
sceneCN: 这里 serene 是「安详的、平静的」（第 1 个义项：心里或环境没有波澜）；句意：喧闹的下午过去后，院子变得安详，孩子们说话都压低了声音。

pos.zh: 晴朗无云的；温和的（多指天气、天空、海面）
宁静的海面；晴空；高贵者（用于称号）

derivatives.zh: 由 serene 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，指「宁静；安详」
由 serene 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，指「安详地；平静地」
由 serene 加 -ness 构成，是 serenity 的对应名词形式，较少用

senses.title: Calm and untroubled in mood
senses.titleCN: 安详的；平静的（心情、神情）
senses.definition: peaceful and untroubled, with no sign of worry or anger
senses.definitionCN: 平和而无忧虑，看不出焦虑或怒气
senses.example: She answered every question with a serene smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个问题都带着安详的微笑作答。
senses.why: The Latin word first describes weather that has cleared, so a cloudless face becomes the earliest figurative sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词最初形容放晴的天气，于是「没有阴云的脸」成为最早的比喻义。

senses.title: Clear and undisturbed weather
senses.titleCN: 晴朗的；无扰的（天空、天气）
senses.definition: clear of cloud, wind or storm, usually of sky and weather
senses.definitionCN: 没有云、风或暴雨，多形容天空与天气
senses.example: The morning was serene, with not a cloud above the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 早晨天气晴朗，海湾上空一片云也没有。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: the sky cleared of storm clouds is the original picture behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：暴风雨云散去的天空，正是这个词背后的原始画面。

senses.title: A calm sea or stretch of water
senses.definition: smooth and still, without waves or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 平滑静止，没有浪涛或扰动
senses.example: We rowed out onto the serene water before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 日出前我们把船划到平静的水面上。
senses.why: Water takes the same calm as sky, so the sea that mirrors a clear sky is called serene.
senses.whyCN: 水面和天空一样可以平静，倒映晴空的海面也就被叫作 serene。

senses.title: Free from disturbance of any kind
senses.titleCN: 宁静的；静谧的（地方、时光）
senses.definition: describing a place or period free from noise, rush or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有噪音、匆忙或冲突的地方或时段
senses.example: The study was a serene room that shut out the street entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 书房是一个完全把街道隔在外面的宁静房间。
senses.why: Once calm moves from weather to people, it readily extends to settings that let that calm arise.
senses.whyCN: 平静一旦从天气转到人身上，就很容易再扩展到能让人平静下来的场所。

senses.title: Mild and graciously quiet in manner
senses.definition: showing gentle, unhurried composure, especially in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 表现出温和而不慌乱的镇定，尤其在难处
senses.example: He stayed serene while the crowd shouted at him.
senses.exampleCN: 人群冲他大喊时，他仍然很从容。
senses.why: Calm under pressure is calm made visible in behaviour, so the weather sense shifts into social poise.
senses.whyCN: 压力之下的平静是看得见的行为，于是天气义就转成了社交场上的从容。

senses.title: A high and gracious title
senses.definition: in ceremonial titles, meaning high, gracious and above all disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 在礼仪称号中表示崇高、仁慈、不受纷扰
senses.example: The envoy was received by His Serene Highness in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 使者上午受到尊贵的殿下接见。
senses.why: Court language borrowed the clear sky as a sign of undisturbed rank, so serenity became part of titles.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷用语借「晴朗天空」象征不受纷扰的尊位，于是宁静之意进入了称号。

senses.title: The calm as a noun
senses.titleCN: 宁静（名词用法，书面、旧式）
senses.definition: the state of being calm and clear, now mainly poetic or archaic
senses.definitionCN: 平静而清朗的状态，如今多用于诗歌或古旧文体
senses.example: The evening serene lay over the valley like a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的宁静像一块布，铺在整个山谷上。
senses.why: A poetic tradition let the adjective stand on its own as a noun, turning the quality into a scene.
senses.whyCN: 诗歌传统让形容词单独作名词用，把这种性质直接变成了一个场景。

senses.title: A serene face as a sign of inner peace
senses.titleCN: 安详的（面容，尤指逝者或修行者）
senses.definition: used of a face or expression that shows deep, lasting inner peace
senses.definitionCN: 形容面容或神情显示出深沉而持久的内心安宁
senses.example: Her grandmother lay with a serene face after a long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 外婆久病之后躺在那儿，面容安详。
senses.why: The sense of an undisturbed surface deepened into a mark of lasting inner peace rather than a passing mood.
senses.whyCN: 「表面不受扰」的意思深化为一种持久的内心平静，而不只是短暂的情绪。

intro.en: Serene comes from Latin serenus, meaning clear, cloudless or calm, a word whose older roots are uncertain; it entered English through Old French and has kept its weather sense beside the emotional one.
intro.cn: serene 来自拉丁语 serenus（清朗、无云、平静），这个词的更古老来源不确定；它经由古法语进入英语，一直把天气义与情绪义并存在一起。

items.en: Serenus describes a clear, cloudless sky or a calm sea.
items.cn: serenus 形容晴朗无云的天空或平静的海面。

items.en: Words such as serus, late, and the root seen in caelum serenum, have been proposed as links, but the etymology is uncertain.
items.cn: 有人提出与表示「晚」的 serus 或「晴朗天空」相关，但词源来源不确定，不宜定论。

items.en: Serain or serein carries the adjective northward.
items.cn: 古法语用 serain（或 serein）把形容词带往北方。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English with both the sky sense and the mood sense.
items.cn: 英语中此词既记有天空义，也记有情绪义。

items.en: Romantic poetry and modern usage reinforce it as a calm, restful descriptive word.
items.cn: 浪漫主义诗歌与现代用法进一步把它固定为表示平静安详的描述词。

note.en: Serene is close to its Latin noun serenity and to other calm words, but it keeps a slightly literary and clear-sky flavour.
note.cn: serene 与同根名词 serenity 及其它表示「静」的词相近，但保留一点文学味和「天空放晴」的色彩。

entries.definition: the state of being calm and untroubled
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指宁静安详的状态。

entries.definition: in a calm and untroubled way
entries.definitionCN: 由 serene 派生而来的副词，指安详地。

entries.definition: grave, solemn or not joking
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自拉丁语 gravis 一路，指严肃。

entries.definition: quiet, still and free from disturbance
entries.definitionCN: 宁静的、没有扰动的，比 serene 更强调静止。

entries.definition: not easily excited, calmly steady
entries.definitionCN: 不易激动的、平静的，多形容人或水面。

entries.definition: full of peace, without conflict or noise
entries.definitionCN: 和平的、安适的，最日常的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Serene pictures weather that has cleared; remember it as a sky with no cloud and a face with no worry.
normalIntro.cn: serene 描绘放晴后的天气：把它记成「没有云的天空 + 没有愁绪的脸」。

normal.en: A serene smile is calm, while an angry smile is not serene at all.
normal.cn: serene smile 是安详的微笑，而愤怒的笑一点也不 serene。

normal.en: The noun serenity means calmness, and the adverb serenely means calmly.
normal.cn: 名词 serenity 表示宁静，副词 serenely 表示平静地。

normal.en: A serene sky is clear of cloud; a serene sea is smooth.
normal.cn: serene sky 是没有云的天空，serene sea 是平滑的海面。

normal.en: Serene often appears in polite descriptions where calm and dignity meet.
normal.cn: serene 常出现在既平静又带尊严的书面描述中。

normal.en: Compare calm: calm is common and plain, serene is slightly literary and brighter.
normal.cn: 对比 calm：calm 日常平实，serene 稍文雅，还带一点明净感。

abstract.en: Think of a lake just after rain, so still that the far shore is mirrored.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后不久的一片湖，静得映出对岸的倒影。

abstract.en: Picture a nurse moving through a ward at night, unhurried and quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位护士夜里在病房中走动，不急也不响。

abstract.en: See a monk breathing slowly beside an open window on a clear morning.
abstract.cn: 想象清早窗边，一位僧人慢慢呼吸。

examples.en: The lake lay serene in the early light.
examples.cn: 晨光里湖面一片平静。

examples.en: She remained serene even when the meeting turned hostile.
examples.cn: 即使会议变得充满敌意，她依然镇静。

examples.en: We spent a serene hour in the garden before the traffic began.
examples.cn: 车流开始前，我们在花园里度过了宁静的一小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色润」——天色润蓝、湖面润亮，没有风也没有云；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 serenus（晴朗的；平静的）→ 古法语 serain → 英语 serene；更古老的词根来源不确定，一般认为与「天气放晴」直接相关。

sensesIntro.en: Serene begins with a clear sky, moves to calm water and quiet places, then to untroubled minds and to high courtly titles.
sensesIntro.cn: serene 从晴朗的天空开始，转到平静的水面与安静的地方，再转到无忧的心绪与高贵的称号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror still lake under a cloudless sky after a storm.
core.cn: 核心意象：暴风雨过后，晴空下如镜的湖面。

branches.en: Clear sky and still water keep the oldest literal sense.
branches.cn: 晴空与静水保留了最古老的字面义。

branches.en: A face can be as cloudless as a sky, from passing calm to lasting peace.
branches.cn: 面容可以像天空一样无云，可以是短暂的一刻安静，也可以是持久的安宁。

branches.en: Composure in action is calm turned into behaviour.
branches.cn: 举止上的镇定是平静转化为行为的样子。

branches.en: Places that allow calm are described by the calm itself.
branches.cn: 能让人安静下来的场所，也被这个词本身来形容。

branches.en: Court titles and poetic nouns extend the word beyond description.
branches.cn: 宫廷称号与诗歌名词把这个词延伸到了描述之外。

intro.en: Serene is a whole Latin borrowing; English builds on it with -ity, -ly and -ness rather than with compound parts.
intro.cn: serene 是整体借入的拉丁词；英语主要用 -ity、-ly、-ness 等后缀在它上面构成新词，而不是拆成复合成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin serenus is a single adjective, and its older root is uncertain, so the Latin family below is small and descriptive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serenus 是一个单形容词，更早的词根不确定，因此下面的拉丁同族词不多，多是描述性的。

items.example: Serenus gives the clearest weather image.
items.exampleCN: serenus 提供了最清楚的天气意象。

items.example: Serenum is the noun behind the weather sense.
items.exampleCN: serenum 是天气义背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms serenity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 serenity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms serenely.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 serenely。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sereneness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 sereneness。

items.example: The ending -er forms serener.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 serener。

items.example: The ending -est forms serenest.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -est 构成 serenest。

items.example: Serain is the Old French link.
items.exampleCN: serain 是古法语的中间形式。

items.example: Calm is the plainer partner of serene.
items.exampleCN: calm 是 serene 更平实的搭档。

definition_zh: 连续的；序列的；分期连载的；连载小说（或节目）；串行数据接口；连续出版物的编号
definition_en: forming a series one after another, published or broadcast in regular parts, or relating to data sent bit by bit in order
core_image: 一节一节连成一串的珠子，每一颗都在前一颗后面
scene: 老收音机里，广播剧每周播一集，听众守着时间等下一段。In the old days, families gathered around the radio for the next episode of their favourite serial.
sceneCN: 这里 serial 是「连载作品、连续剧」（第 2 个义项：分期播出的故事）；句意：从前一家人围着收音机，等他们最爱的那部连续剧下一集。

pos.zh: 连续的；按顺序的；序列的
分期连载的；连续播出的
连载小说；连续剧；连续出版物
串行的（数据一位一位依次传送）

derivatives.zh: 同源名词，指「一连串；系列；丛书」，是语义词根的直接体现
由 serial 加动词后缀 -ise 构成，指「使成连载；连载出版」
由 serialise 再接 -ation 构成，指「连载；连续化」
由 serial 加 -ly 构成，指「连续地；按顺序地」
由 serial 加 -ness 构成的稀有名词，指「连续的性质」

senses.title: Arranged one after another
senses.definition: happening or arranged in a series, with each item following the one before
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序发生或排列，每一项都紧跟在前一项之后
senses.example: The files are named in serial order from one to ninety.
senses.exampleCN: 这些文件从一到九十按顺序编号命名。
senses.why: Latin serere means to join in a row, so the core image is items strung one after another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 serere 意为「串成一行」，核心意象就是一项接一项串起来。

senses.title: Published or broadcast in parts
senses.titleCN: 分期连载的；连续播出的
senses.definition: issued in a number of separate parts that appear at regular intervals
senses.definitionCN: 分成若干部分，在固定时间隔间陆续刊出或播出
senses.example: The novel first appeared as a serial in a monthly magazine.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说最初以连载形式登在月刊上。
senses.why: The row of beads becomes a row of episodes, so serial means a story delivered part by part.
senses.whyCN: 一串珠子变成了一串情节，于是 serial 指按分段呈现的故事。

senses.title: A story told in instalments
senses.definition: a story, play or programme presented in regular instalments
senses.definitionCN: 按固定分段讲述的小说、戏剧或节目
senses.example: We watched the whole serial over one rainy weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 我们用一个下雨的周末把这部连续剧全看完了。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun by ellipsis: a serial story simply became a serial.
senses.whyCN: 形容词通过省略变成了名词：连载体故事直接简称 serial。

senses.title: Repeated as a pattern
senses.titleCN: 重复发生的；连续不断的
senses.definition: used of events or people that keep repeating in the same pattern
senses.definitionCN: 形容以同一模式不断重复的事件或人
senses.example: Police linked the thefts to a serial offender.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把这些盗窃案与一名连环作案者联系起来。
senses.why: From a row of objects the word grows to a row of acts, so repetition becomes the defining feature.
senses.whyCN: 从一排物件扩展到一连串行为，于是「重复」成了这个义项的核心特征。

senses.title: One bit at a time in data
senses.definition: sending data one bit at a time over a single line, in sequence
senses.definitionCN: 数据在一个通道上一位一位依次传送
senses.example: The printer still connects through a serial port.
senses.exampleCN: 这台打印机仍然通过串行端口连接。
senses.why: Serial keeps its row image in computing, where bits travel one after another instead of side by side.
senses.whyCN: 在计算机领域，serial 仍保留「排队」意象：数据位依次通过，而不是并排传送。

senses.title: Identified by a running number
senses.definition: of a number, given in sequence to identify a single manufactured item
senses.definitionCN: 指按顺序给出、用于识别单件产品的编号
senses.example: Write down the serial number on the back of the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 请记下机器背面的序号。
senses.why: A row of numbers is the plainest row of all, so serial labels the counting marks of things made alike.
senses.whyCN: 一排数字是最朴素的一排，于是 serial 用来指同类产品上逐个递增的编号。

senses.title: A journal or numbered publication
senses.definition: a periodical or other publication that appears in numbered issues under one title
senses.definitionCN: 同一标题下按编号连续出版的期刊或其它刊物
senses.example: The library files the journal as a serial, not a book.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆把这份期刊归为连续出版物，而不是书。
senses.why: Library cataloguing follows the row of issues, so anything issued in a numbered succession is a serial.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆编目依据的是「一期接一期」，所以凡是按编号连续发行的都算 serial。

senses.title: Taking turns in a single channel
senses.titleCN: 依次的；轮流进行的（非并行）
senses.definition: done by turns rather than at the same time, often contrasted with parallel
senses.definitionCN: 轮流进行而非同时进行，常与「并行」相对
senses.example: Students take the listening test on serial machines.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在依次安排的机器上做听力测试。
senses.why: Serial contrasts with parallel by insisting on order: one thing, then the next, never all together.
senses.whyCN: serial 与「并行」相对，强调先后：一件做完再做下一件，从不同时。

intro.en: Serial comes from Latin series, a row or chain, from serere, to join or bind together; English formed the adjective with -al in the seventeenth century, and the modern senses grew from row, to instalments, to numbers and data.
intro.cn: serial 来自拉丁语 series（一排、链），源于 serere（连接、串起）；英语在十七世纪加上 -al 构成形容词，后来又沿着「一排」衍生出连载、编号与数据等义。

items.en: Serere means to join, weave or string together.
items.cn: serere 意为连接、编织、串成一串。

items.en: Series is a row, a chain or an order of things.
items.cn: series 指一排、一串或有秩序的顺序。

items.en: The suffix -al forms the adjective serial from series.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 把 series 变成形容词 serial。

items.en: Serial describes stories issued part by part and identical items by running number.
items.cn: serial 开始形容分期发表的故事，以及带流水号的同类物品。

items.en: Computing adds serial ports and serial data, and crime reporting adds the serial offender.
items.cn: 计算机领域带来串行端口与串行数据，犯罪报道带来「连环作案者」。

note.en: Serial shares its Latin row with series and stresses one-after-another order; it sits close to episode words and to the opposite word parallel.
note.cn: serial 与 series 同出自拉丁语「一排」，强调「一项接一项」的次序；它与表示「集」的词以及反义的 parallel 相邻。

entries.definition: a number of things or events in a row
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，指一连串事物或事件。

entries.definition: one after another in order
entries.definitionCN: 由 serial 派生的副词，指「依次地」。

entries.definition: a breakfast food made from grain
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：它来自罗马谷物女神刻瑞斯之名，指谷类早餐食品。

entries.definition: following in a logical or fixed order
entries.definitionCN: 近义且更正式，强调有固定先后次序。

entries.definition: a single broadcast instalment of a series
entries.definitionCN: 一集，是 serial 的一小段。

entries.definition: happening at the same time on separate channels
entries.definitionCN: 反义对照词，指几条通道同时并行处理。

normalIntro.en: Serial is a row of beads: the Latin root ser- gathers things in a line, and every new sense adds another bead.
normalIntro.cn: serial 是一串珠子：拉丁词根 ser- 把东西串成一条线，每长出新的义项就多穿一颗珠子。

normal.en: A serial number is a running number on a product label.
normal.cn: serial number 是产品标签上的流水号。

normal.en: A serial killer acts again and again in a pattern.
normal.cn: serial killer 是反复按同一模式作案的人。

normal.en: Series shares its root: one series, many serials, all in a row.
normal.cn: series 与它同根：一个系列、若干连载，都排在一行里。

normal.en: The verb serialise means to publish something in parts.
normal.cn: 动词 serialise 意为「连载出版」。

normal.en: Compare serial with parallel: serial goes one after another, parallel goes together.
normal.cn: 对比 serial 与 parallel：一个依次进行，一个同时进行。

abstract.en: Picture a string of beads, each touching the next, with no gaps.
abstract.cn: 想象一串珠子，颗颗相连，中间没有空隙。

abstract.en: Imagine an evening radio hour that stops halfway and leaves you waiting a week.
abstract.cn: 想象一个傍晚的广播时段，正讲到一半就停了，让你再等一周。

abstract.en: Think of a ticket counter where one clerk serves one queue, then the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一个窗口，只有一个职员，先服务这一列，再服务下一列。

examples.en: The magazine ran the story as a serial over six months.
examples.cn: 这家杂志用六个月把故事分期连载完。

examples.en: Every device carries a serial number printed on its back.
examples.cn: 每台设备背面都印有一个序列号。

examples.en: In serial transmission, the bits travel one at a time.
examples.cn: 在串行传输中，数据位一位一位地传送。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色瑞奥」——像夜里一集接一集地追剧，色块一样一段接一段亮着；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 serere（连接、串起）→ series（一排；一连串）→ 英语加 -al 得 serial，核心义「一项接一项地排下去」。

sensesIntro.en: Serial starts from a simple row, becomes a story in parts, then a running number, and finally a technical contrast with parallel.
sensesIntro.cn: serial 从简单的一排出发，变成分段的故事、流水号，最后成为与「并行」相对的技术术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: beads strung one behind another, each touching the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗接一颗串起来的珠子。

branches.en: The plain row splits into fixed order and take-turns order.
branches.cn: 朴素的一排分化为固定次序与轮流次序。

branches.en: A row of parts becomes a serial story and then the serial itself.
branches.cn: 一排分段变成连载故事，再变成名词性的「连载作品」。

branches.en: A row of acts produces the serial offender.
branches.cn: 一连串行为产生了「连环作案者」。

branches.en: A row of bits and bytes makes the technical serial channel.
branches.cn: 一排排的数据位构成了技术上的串行通道。

branches.en: Numbered labels and numbered issues both keep the row.
branches.cn: 编号标签与编号期刊都保有「一排」的意象。

intro.en: Serial is built from the Latin root ser- plus the adjective suffix -al, and English then adds -ise, -ation, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: serial 由拉丁词根 ser- 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，英语随后又加上 -ise、-ation、-ly、-ness 等后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on serere, to join, with seri- as the stem that reaches English through series and serial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族建立在 serere（连接）之上，词干 seri- 经由 series 与 serial 进入英语。

items.meaning: to join, weave or string together
items.example: Serere gives the image of joining in a line.
items.exampleCN: serere 提供「连成一行」的意象。

items.meaning: a row, a chain, a succession
items.example: Series passes straight into English as a noun.
items.exampleCN: series 直接作为名词进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -al turns series into serial.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 把 series 变成 serial。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms serially.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 serially。

items.meaning: to make or to turn into
items.example: The suffix -ise forms serialise.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 构成 serialise。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms serialisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 serialisation。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms serialness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 serialness。

items.meaning: beside, alongside, as a contrast to serial order
items.meaningCN: 旁边；并排（对照串行的术语来源）
items.example: The prefix par- gives the opposite idea in parallel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 par- 在 parallel 中给出相反的概念。

items.example: The word port pairs with serial in serial port.
items.exampleCN: port 与 serial 组成 serial port 这一术语。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被连接起来的；串起来的

definition_zh: 蛇（尤指大蛇）；毒蛇；阴险狡猾的人；蛇形饰物
definition_en: a snake, especially a large or dangerous one, or a person imagined as sly and treacherous; also a winding shape or ornament
core_image: 一条细长的身体贴着地面盘成螺旋，蜿蜒前行而不发出声响
scene: 旧书里画着一条绕着果树的蛇，孩子们盯着那幅图不敢翻页。In the old book a serpent curled around the fruit tree, and the children were afraid to turn the page.
sceneCN: 这里 serpent 是「蛇」（第 1 个义项：蛇，尤指体型大或危险的蛇）；句意：旧书里画着一条绕着果树的蛇，孩子们不敢翻页。

pos.zh: 蛇形的；蜿蜒的（多用于固定说法）

collocations.zh: 花园里的蛇（喻引诱人堕落的阴险者）
铜蛇（宗教典故中的铜制蛇像）
蛇一般的低语；阴险的教唆

derivatives.zh: 由 serpent 加形容词尾构成，义为「蜿蜒的；蛇形的」，也作名词指蛇纹石
由形容词转成的动词，义为「蛇行；蜿蜒前进」，多用于文学描写
由 serpent 加副词尾构成，义为「像蛇一样地」，属罕用的文学写法

senses.title: A snake, especially a large one
senses.definition: a snake, especially a large or impressive one, often used in literary or biblical contexts
senses.definitionCN: 蛇，尤指体型较大、令人印象深刻的蛇，多用于文学或经典语境
senses.example: A huge serpent lay coiled beneath the palm.
senses.exampleCN: 一条巨蛇盘在棕榈树下。
senses.why: Latin serpens is the present participle of serpere, to creep, so the word names the creature by the way it moves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 serpens 是 serpere（爬行）的现在分词，这个词是用「爬行的动作」给这种动物命名。

senses.title: A venomous and dangerous snake
senses.definition: a snake that bites and can kill, usually read as a threat or an evil omen
senses.definitionCN: 会咬人并致命的蛇，通常被理解为威胁或凶兆
senses.example: The villagers feared the serpents in the reeds.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们害怕芦苇丛里的毒蛇。
senses.why: Because creeping serpents strike without warning, the word carries fear from the very start.
senses.whyCN: 因为爬行的蛇往往毫无预兆地出击，这个词从一开始就带着恐惧的色彩。

senses.title: A sly and treacherous person
senses.definition: a person who is cunning or deceitful and harms others while seeming harmless
senses.definitionCN: 狡诈或善于欺骗、表面无害却伤害他人的人
senses.example: People called the smooth-talking agent a serpent.
senses.exampleCN: 人们说那个口蜜腹剑的代理人是个阴险小人。
senses.why: The biblical serpent that lured the first couple out of the garden fixed the snake as the image of quiet malice.
senses.whyCN: 经典叙事中引诱第一对夫妇离开乐园的那条蛇，把蛇固定成「安静的恶意」的意象。

senses.title: A winding shape or ornament
senses.definition: something shaped like a snake, such as a winding line or a coiled decoration
senses.definitionCN: 形状像蛇的东西，如蜿蜒的线条或盘曲的装饰
senses.example: The fountain is carved with a bronze serpent.
senses.exampleCN: 那座喷泉上雕着一条青铜蛇。
senses.why: Once the shape has a name, any curl or coil can borrow it and become a useful decorative image.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种形状有了名字，任何弯曲盘绕之物都能借用它，成为好用的装饰意象。

senses.title: A firework or weapon named after the snake
senses.definition: a type of firework or old weapon that moves in a wriggling track, named after the animal
senses.definitionCN: 一种沿扭动轨迹飞行或移动的烟花或旧式兵器，因形似爬蛇而得名
senses.example: Fireworks crackled and serpents darted across the night sky.
senses.exampleCN: 烟花劈啪作响，蛇形火星在夜空中乱窜。
senses.why: Manufacturers of firecrackers and early guns borrowed the animal name for anything that darted forward.
senses.whyCN: 烟花与早期枪炮的制造者借用了动物名，来称呼会一条条窜出去的东西。

intro.en: Serpent comes from Latin serpens, a creeping thing, the participle of serpere, to creep or crawl, and reached English through Old French serpent.
intro.cn: serpent 来自拉丁语 serpens（爬行之物），它是动词 serpere（爬行）的分词，经古法语 serpent 进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root serp, meaning to creep or crawl, lies behind the family.
items.cn: 这一词族可追溯到重构形式 serp，意为「爬行」。

items.en: The verb serpere means to creep, and its participle serpens gives the noun serpens, a creeping thing.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 serpere 意为爬行，其分词 serpens 构成名词 serpens，即「爬行之物」。

items.en: Old French respells the noun as serpent, keeping both the animal and the creeping picture.
items.cn: 古法语把该名词写作 serpent，既保留了动物义，也保留了爬行的意象。

items.en: English borrows the word through the French Bible and romance texts.
items.cn: 英语通过法语圣经与传奇故事文献借入这个词。

items.en: The adjective form hangs on in phrasal terms such as the Serpentine river and works as a curving decor word.
items.cn: 其形容词形态保留在 Serpentine 河这类固定说法中，并成为描写曲线装饰的用词。

note.en: Serpent links to the Latin creeping root in serpentine and to the plain word for the animal, snake.
note.cn: serpent 既与 serpentine 共享拉丁语「爬行」词根，也与表示这种动物的普通词 snake 相邻。

entries.definition: winding like a snake
entries.definitionCN: 像蛇一样蜿蜒的；与 serpent 共享拉丁词根

entries.definition: a creeping thing, in Latin
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「爬行之物」，是 serpent 的直接来源

entries.definition: to move slowly with the body close to the ground
entries.definitionCN: 匍匐爬行；只是本义相近，拼写与词源都与 serpent 无关

entries.definition: a long thin animal without legs
entries.definitionCN: 蛇；最普通的说法，serpent 更书面、更具文学色彩

entries.definition: a poisonous snake, or a spiteful person
entries.definitionCN: 毒蛇；也指恶毒的人，比 serpent 更明确指有毒种类

entries.definition: a very large snake that crushes its prey
entries.definitionCN: 巨蟒；是蛇的一类，来源为希腊神话中的大蛇名

normalIntro.en: Serpent is the literary snake: its name is simply the creature that creeps.
normalIntro.cn: serpent 是书面语里的蛇：名字本身就来自「爬行」这个动作。

normal.en: Serpent and serpentine share one root, so a serpentine road is a road that crawls.
normal.cn: serpent 与 serpentine 同根，所以「蛇形的路」就是蜿蜒爬行的路。

normal.en: Snake is the everyday word, serpent is the word of Bibles, poems, and myth.
normal.cn: snake 是日常说法，serpent 属于圣经、诗歌与神话的语域。

normal.en: A venomous serpent bites without warning, so the word also means a sly enemy.
normal.cn: 毒蛇咬人毫无预兆，所以这个词也指阴险的敌人。

normal.en: Coil, creep, and hiss all belong to the serpent s world of quiet movement.
normal.cn: coil、creep、hiss 这些词都属于 serpent 那种安静移动的世界。

normal.en: The Latin participle serpens shows the pattern of other animal words named by their motion.
normal.cn: 拉丁语分词 serpens 体现了「按动作给动物命名」的构词方式。

abstract.en: Picture a long body sliding over stones, its belly moving in small waves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细长的身体滑过石块，腹部一浪一浪地向前送。

abstract.en: Imagine a coiled shadow at the foot of a tree, barely visible in the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象树根下有一团盘着的影子，在草里几乎看不见。

abstract.en: See a smiling face whose words twist away from what the person really means.
abstract.cn: 想象一张带笑的脸，说出的话却总绕着真实意图打转。

examples.en: An old legend tells of a serpent that guarded the well.
examples.cn: 古老传说讲一条蛇守护着这口井。

examples.en: The river takes a serpentine course through the valley.
examples.cn: 这条河在谷地上蜿蜒流过。

examples.en: In the story the serpent whispers advice that the hero should not trust.
examples.cn: 故事里的那条蛇低声出着主意，英雄不该相信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「蛇盘特」——蛇把身体盘得特别紧，正好对应 serpent 盘曲的形象；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 serpens（爬行之物）← serpere（爬行）→ 古法语 serpent → 英语 serpent，核心义「贴着地面爬行的长条生物」。

sensesIntro.en: Serpent starts as the literary name of the creeping animal, gains its menace and human metaphor, and finally extends to any winding shape.
sensesIntro.cn: serpent 先指文学语境里爬行的动物，随后带上威胁与人类比喻，最后扩展到一切蛇形之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long body coiled on the ground, moving without a sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具盘在地上的细长身体，无声地移动。

branches.en: The literary name for the animal is the base sense.
branches.cn: 书面语里指这种动物，是基础义项。

branches.en: The dangerous snake is the feared, venomous version of the animal.
branches.cn: 危险的毒蛇是动物义项中令人畏惧的一面。

branches.en: A cunning enemy borrows the snake that strikes from hiding.
branches.cn: 阴险的敌人借用了从暗处出击的蛇的形象。

branches.en: Any curving line or carved coil can take the snake shape.
branches.cn: 任何弯曲的线条或盘绕的雕刻都能借用蛇形。

branches.en: Fireworks and old weapons that dart and wriggle are named after the living snake.
branches.cn: 会窜动扭行的烟花与旧兵器，正是照活蛇的样子命名的。

intro.en: Serpent belongs to a small Latin family built on the creeping verb serpere, with English serpentine as its main extended form.
intro.cn: serpent 属于以拉丁语爬行动词 serpere 为核心的小词族，英语中主要的延伸形式是 serpentine。

latinIntro.en: Latin serpere means to creep, and the participle serpens turned the action into the name of a creature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serpere 意为爬行，其分词 serpens 把动作变成了动物的名字。

items.example: Serpere supplies the creeping image behind the word.
items.exampleCN: serpere 提供这个词背后的爬行意象。

items.example: Serpens is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: serpens 是英语单词的直接祖先。

items.example: Serpent keeps the formal, literary tone of the borrowing.
items.exampleCN: serpent 保留了借词正式、文学化的语气。

items.meaningCN: 正在做某事者（分词词尾）
items.example: The ending -ent turns a verb into the doer of the action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 把动词变成动作的执行者。

items.example: Serpentine describes paths, rivers, and dances.
items.exampleCN: serpentine 常用来形容小路、河流与舞步。

items.example: The suffix -ine links the animal to the shape it makes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ine 把动物与其造成的形状联系起来。

items.example: The suffix -ly can form the rare literary adverb serpently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 可构成罕用的文学副词 serpently。

items.example: Serpently appears mostly in poetry and old prose.
items.exampleCN: serpently 主要出现在诗歌与旧式散文里。

items.example: Sinister describes similar omens but has a different root.
items.exampleCN: sinister 描述类似的凶兆，但词根并不相同。

definition_zh: 芝麻；芝麻籽；芝麻油
definition_en: a small flat oil seed of a tropical plant, used in cooking and baking, or the plant that produces it
core_image: 一小把扁平的浅色小籽，在指尖轻轻一捏就露出油光
scene: 面包铺的柜台上摆着一袋散装芝麻，顾客用勺子舀进纸袋。At the bakery counter a jar of sesame stood open, and the customer scooped some into a paper bag.
sceneCN: 这里 sesame 是「芝麻」（第 1 个义项：芝麻籽，一种小巧扁平的油脂种子）；句意：面包铺柜台上摆着一袋散装的芝麻，顾客用勺子舀进纸袋。

derivatives.zh: 由 sesame 与 seed 复合再加过去分词词尾构成，义为「撒了芝麻的」，多指面包
与 sesame 同源的希腊语 sesamoeides（像芝麻的）构成的形容词，解剖学义为「籽骨状的」
由 sesame 加化学名词尾 -in 构成，义为「芝麻素」，一种存在于芝麻中的成分

senses.title: The small oil seed
senses.definition: a small flat seed with a nutty flavour, used on bread, in sweets, and pressed for oil
senses.definitionCN: 一种小而扁、带坚果香味的种子，用于面包与糕点，也可榨油
senses.example: She sprinkled sesame over the warm bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她在热面包上撒了芝麻。
senses.why: The word names the seed itself, and English kept the plant name for the tiny product people actually handle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本指植株，但英语用它来称呼人们真正接触的那一粒粒小小的种子。

senses.title: The plant that bears the seed
senses.definition: a tropical plant grown for its seeds, with tall stems and small white or pinkish flowers
senses.definitionCN: 为取籽而种植的热带植物，茎秆高直，开白色或淡粉色小花
senses.example: Farmers in the region grow sesame in fields after the rains.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的农民在雨后于田里种芝麻。
senses.why: The crop sense is the original one, because the plant arrived in English as an exotic import.
senses.whyCN: 作物义才是本义，因为这种植物最初是作为异域作物进入英语的。

senses.title: The oil pressed from the seed
senses.definition: the oil pressed from sesame seeds, used in cooking and in dressings
senses.definitionCN: 用芝麻籽榨出的油，用于烹调与调味
senses.example: A spoon of sesame gives the noodles a deep nutty aroma.
senses.exampleCN: 一勺香油让面条带上一股深沉的坚果香。
senses.why: Since the seed belongs to the kitchen, its oil is often called by the same short name.
senses.whyCN: 种子本来就属于厨房，榨出的油也常直接用同一个名称来指代。

senses.title: A password meaning in the talisman tale
senses.definition: the secret word that opens a sealed door in the well-known tale of a magic cave
senses.definitionCN: 著名魔术洞穴故事中用来打开石门的神秘咒语
senses.example: The children shouted the word sesame at the rock and waited.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对着岩石喊出「芝麻」的口令，然后等着。
senses.why: Translators borrowed an old spelling of the plant name as a password, and English kept the pun as a set phrase.
senses.whyCN: 译者把植物名的一个古老拼写借来当口令，英语又把这个双关保留成固定说法。

intro.en: Sesame came to English through Latin and Greek from a Semitic word, with an early form that the translators of the famous tale turned into an opening charm.
intro.cn: sesame 经拉丁语与希腊语来自闪米特语词，其早期拼写被著名故事的译者改造成开门口的咒语。

items.en: Semitic languages used forms such as sumsumu and shumshunu for the oil-bearing plant.
items.cn: 闪米特语族用 sumsumu、shumshunu 一类词形称呼这种含油植物。

items.en: Greek borrowed the plant as sesamon and sesamis, the sesame seed.
items.cn: 希腊语借入为 sesamon 与 sesamis，指芝麻籽。

items.en: Latin sesamum carries the same plant name into European uses.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sesamum 把同一植物名带入欧洲各地。

items.en: English adopts sesame as a name for the plant and its seed.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪左右用 sesame 称呼这种植物及其种子。

items.en: European translators of an Arabic tale turned the old word shumshunu into the magic phrase that opens a rock door.
items.cn: 欧洲译者翻译一则阿拉伯故事时，把旧词形 shumshunu 改成了能打开岩门的咒语。

note.en: Sesame is a plant word with no English root family, so it is compared with everyday seeds and with familiar seed-named tales.
note.cn: sesame 是一个没有英语词族的植物词，所以拿来与常见种子词和以种子命名的故事比较。

entries.definition: the Latin plant name behind sesame
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语植物名，是 sesame 的直接来源

entries.definition: an early Semitic word for sesame linked to the magic phrase
entries.definitionCN: 早期闪米特语词形，与故事中的开门咒语有关

entries.definition: shaped like a sesame seed, said of small bones
entries.definitionCN: 籽骨状的；用希腊语「像芝麻的」构成，与 sesame 同源

entries.definition: a plant whose tiny seeds go on bread and cakes
entries.definitionCN: 罂粟；籽常撒在面包与蛋糕上，与芝麻常当配角

entries.definition: a yellow seed paste used as a sharp condiment
entries.definitionCN: 芥末；同样是见于餐桌的小籽调味料

entries.definition: a tall plant grown for oil and edible seeds
entries.definitionCN: 向日葵；也是以榨油为主的作物种子

normalIntro.en: Sesame is a borrowed plant name, so the trick is to learn it as a kitchen word and a story word at once.
normalIntro.cn: sesame 是借入的植物名，记忆的关键是同时把它当作厨房词与故事词。

normal.en: Sesame is both the seed on bread and the plant in the field, so one word covers crop and kitchen.
normal.cn: sesame 既是面包上的籽，也是田里的作物，一个词同时覆盖农田与厨房。

normal.en: Sesame oil is the thick nutty oil used in noodle dishes and dressings.
normal.cn: sesame oil 就是拌面与凉菜里那种醇厚的香油。

normal.en: Sesame paste is a common spread and soup base in daily cooking.
normal.cn: sesame paste 是家常做酱与调汤底的常用材料。

normal.en: The magic phrase in the cave tale comes from an older spelling of this plant name.
normal.cn: 洞穴故事里的那句咒语，其实来自这个词更早的拼写。

normal.en: The Greek form sesamon is the bridge from Semitic words to the English spelling.
normal.cn: 希腊语形式 sesamon 是闪米特语词与英语拼写之间的桥梁。

abstract.en: Imagine tipping a paper packet and letting a hundred tiny seeds slide onto your palm.
abstract.cn: 想象倒转一只纸包，上百粒小小的种子滑到掌心。

abstract.en: See a field of tall stems after the rain, rows of tiny flowers opening in the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后的田里立着一排排高茎，小花在阳光下展开。

abstract.en: Hear a stern voice say the word and a rock door swing back with a low rumble.
abstract.cn: 想象一个低沉的声音念出这个词，岩门伴着闷响缓缓退开。

examples.en: The chef toasted the sesame before adding it to the salad.
examples.cn: 主厨把芝麻烘香后再拌进沙拉。

examples.en: In many kitchens sesame is the base of a rich, nutty dressing.
examples.cn: 在许多厨房里，芝麻是做出浓郁坚果味酱汁的基底。

examples.en: The old story made the word sesame famous as a way of opening a hidden door.
examples.cn: 那个古老的故事让这个植物词成了打开暗门的代名词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞籽米」——把籽粒塞进袋里的米状小粒，正是芝麻的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 闪米特语族词形（如阿卡德语 sumsumu、腓尼基语 shumshunu）→ 希腊语 sesamon、sesamis → 拉丁语 sesamum → 英语 sesame，核心义「含油的小籽植物」。

sensesIntro.en: Sesame names the plant, then the seed people cook with, then its oil, and finally the word became a magic password.
sensesIntro.cn: sesame 先指植株，再指厨房里用的种子，然后是榨出的油，最后这个词本身变成了人名均知的开门暗号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of tiny pale seeds shining with oil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小把泛着油光的浅色小籽。

branches.en: The edible seed is the sense most people meet first.
branches.cn: 可食用的种子是大多数人最先接触的义项。

branches.en: The plant sense is the original crop meaning.
branches.cn: 植株义是最初的作物含义。

branches.en: The oil is the seed pressed into a liquid for cooking.
branches.cn: 油是种子压榨成的烹调液体。

branches.en: The tale sense shows how a plant name became a magic word.
branches.cn: 故事义展示了植物名如何变成一句咒语。

branches.en: Seed and oil are one kitchen chain, from the dry grain to the poured drop.
branches.cn: 籽与油是同一条厨房链条，从干粒一直走到滴出的油。

intro.en: Sesame is not a Latin root word, so it has no productive English affix family, and only its scientific compounds are worth noting.
intro.cn: sesame 不是拉丁词根词，没有能产英语词缀的词族，只有少数科学复合词值得注意。

latinIntro.en: The word passed through Latin sesamum but began in Semitic languages, which is why English built no affix family from it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经过拉丁语 sesamum，但源头在闪米特语，因此英语没能围绕它构成词缀词族。

items.example: Latin sesamum is the form English finally adopted.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 sesamum 是英语最终采用的词形。

items.example: Sesame entered English as an unchanging plant name.
items.exampleCN: sesame 作为植物名进入英语，形态基本不变。

items.example: Anatomy uses sesamoid for small bones near joints.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学用 sesamoid 指关节附近的小骨。

items.example: The suffix -oid builds words that describe shapes.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成描写形状的词。

items.meaning: a compound found in sesame oil
items.meaningCN: 芝麻中的一种成分，芝麻素
items.example: Sesamin is studied for its antioxidant effects.
items.exampleCN: 芝麻素因其抗氧化作用而被研究。

items.example: The suffix -in marks many plant chemicals.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -in 常见于植物化学物质的名称。

items.meaning: a small bone set in a tendon
items.example: The kneecap is a well-known sesamoid bone.
items.exampleCN: 膝盖骨就是常见的籽骨。

items.meaning: a way of getting into a place
items.example: The phrase open sesame comes from the tale.
items.exampleCN: 「开门咒」这一说法就来自那则故事。

items.meaning: a well-known children s television programme
items.meaningCN: 一档著名的儿童电视节目名
items.example: Sesame was chosen for the title of that programme.
items.exampleCN: 那档节目用到了 sesame 这个植物名作为标题。

definition_zh: 污水；下水道污水；污物
definition_en: the dirty water and waste matter carried away from homes and streets through drains and sewers
core_image: 一排深埋地下的管道里，混着洗菜水与污物的暗色水流向下游流去
scene: 河边的管道一开，污水就涌进浅滩，露营的人立刻收拾东西离开。When the pipe opened by the river, sewage poured into the shallows and the campers packed up at once.
sceneCN: 这里 sewage 是「污水」（第 1 个义项：从住宅和街道经下水道排走的脏水与污物）；句意：河边的管道一打开，污水就涌进浅滩，露营的人立刻收拾东西离开。

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: sewer 是 sewage 的词根名词，义为「下水道；阴沟」，污水经由 sewer 排走，加了 -age 才指排走的脏水本身
由 sewer 加 -age 构成，义为「下水道系统；污水排放设施」，侧重系统本身而非污水
sewer 亦作定语修饰名词，如「下水道管」「排污渠道」；与 sewage 的分工是：前者说设施，后者说污水本身

senses.title: Dirty water from homes and streets
senses.definition: the waste water that comes from kitchens, bathrooms, and streets and is carried away in drains
senses.definitionCN: 来自厨房、浴室与街道、经下水道排走的废污水
senses.example: Untreated sewage flows straight into the river.
senses.exampleCN: 未经处理的污水直接流进河里。
senses.why: The suffix -age in French and English marks a mass that has been gathered and carried, so sewage is the collected flow that the sewers remove.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -age 在法语与英语中表示被收集搬运之物，所以 sewage 就是被下水道收走的污水流。

senses.title: The waste matter carried away
senses.definition: the solid and semisolid waste that travels in the same drains as household water
senses.definitionCN: 与生活污水走同一套管道排走的固态或半固态污物
senses.example: Engineers monitor the sewage that passes through the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师监测流经处理厂的污物。
senses.why: Once the word names what flows in the pipes, it covers every kind of waste found there, not only water.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指管道里流动的东西，就涵盖了其中所有类型的废物，而不只是水。

senses.title: The water entering a treatment plant
senses.definition: the incoming dirty water that a treatment works receives and cleans before release
senses.definitionCN: 污水处理厂接收并在排放前净化处理的来水
senses.example: The new plant can handle the sewage of a small city.
senses.exampleCN: 新厂一天能处理一座小城的污水。
senses.why: Modern engineering named the input stream after the whole system, so sewage becomes a quantity that plants measure and clean.
senses.whyCN: 现代工程用整套系统的名称来称呼进水，于是 sewage 成了处理厂需要计量和净化的一股流量。

senses.title: Pollution carried into water
senses.definition: sewage seen as a source of pollution when it enters rivers, lakes, or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 当污水流入河、湖或海时，被看作一种污染源
senses.example: Health inspectors blamed the sewage for the closed beach.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生检查员把海滩关闭归因于污水。
senses.why: The word gains the collective sense of a threat because its presence in water is measured as harm.
senses.whyCN: 因为污水出现在水里时被当作危害来测量，这个词也就获得了「一种威胁」的集合含义。

senses.title: A metaphor for moral waste
senses.definition: a figurative use that pictures corruption or harmful ideas as waste flushing through a society
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性用法，把腐败或有害思想想象成在社会中冲刷而过的污物
senses.example: The novelist described propaganda as the sewage of the public mind.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家把宣传比作公众头脑里的污水。
senses.why: A system that quietly carries away what nobody wants is a ready image for hidden, spreading harm.
senses.whyCN: 一套悄悄运走人人厌恶之物的系统，很容易被借来比喻隐藏而扩散的危害。

intro.en: Sewage is a fairly recent English word, formed from sewer plus the suffix -age in the nineteenth century, and both words go back through Old French to Latin exaqua, to drain water out.
intro.cn: sewage 是相对晚近的英语词，十九世纪由 sewer 加词尾 -age 构成；sewer 与 -age 都经古法语上溯至拉丁语 exaqua（排走水）。

items.en: The colloquial Latin exaqua means to drain out or carry water away.
items.cn: 口语拉丁语 exaqua 意为「排水；把水引走」。

items.en: The verb essuever, from exaqua, means to drain, and its derived noun names the channel that drains.
items.cn: 由 exaqua 来的古法语动词 essuever 意为排水，其派生名词指起排水作用的沟渠。

items.en: English adopts sewer for a drain or ditch, first for draining land and later for removing household waste.
items.cn: 英语借入 sewer 指排水沟，先用于排干土地，后用于排走生活污物。

items.en: Latin-derived sewage appears in early use for the slow discharge of water; the sense of filthy water develops later.
items.cn: 由拉丁语派生的早期词形先指水的缓慢排出，脏水义则更晚才出现。

items.en: Industrial cities needed public drains, and the new word sewage settled on the dirty water carried by those drains.
items.cn: 工业城市需要公共排水，新的 sewage 逐步固定在「由这些管道排走的脏水」这一含义上。

note.en: Sewage pairs with sewer and sewerage, and belongs to the wider field of drains, waste, and water treatment.
note.cn: sewage 与 sewer、sewerage 成组，同属排水、废弃物与水处理的概念域。

entries.definition: an underground pipe that carries waste water
entries.definitionCN: 地下排污管道；是 sewage 的词根名词

entries.definition: the system of drains and the waste flowing in them
entries.definitionCN: 下水道系统；与 sewage 拼写相近但侧重设施体系

entries.definition: the act of stitching cloth
entries.definitionCN: 缝纫；只是拼写相近，与「排水」毫无词源关联

entries.definition: liquid waste flowing out of a plant or works
entries.definitionCN: 废水；多为工业或处理厂排出的液体，比 sewage 更技术化

entries.definition: thick wet waste left after treatment
entries.definitionCN: 污泥；处理污水后留下的浓稠沉淀物

entries.definition: used water from households or industry
entries.definitionCN: 废水；涵盖范围更广，包括不含粪污的废水

normalIntro.en: Sewage is sewer plus -age: the -age suffix turns a channel into the stuff the channel carries.
normalIntro.cn: sewage 是 sewer 加 -age：-age 这个词尾把「管道」变成了「管道里流的东西」。

normal.en: Sewer is the pipe, sewage is what runs inside it.
normal.cn: sewer 是管道，sewage 是管道里流动的污水。

normal.en: The suffix -age marks a collected mass, as in luggage and rubbish.
normal.cn: 词尾 -age 表示成堆收集之物，luggage、rubbish 都是这个理。

normal.en: Sewage treatment means cleaning the water before it goes back to a river.
normal.cn: sewage treatment 就是把水净化后再送回河流。

normal.en: Sewage works is the plant, sewage sludge is what is left over after cleaning.
normal.cn: sewage works 是处理厂，sewage sludge 是净化后剩下的污泥。

normal.en: Old French essuever, to drain, is the distant ancestor of both sewer and sewage.
normal.cn: 古法语 essuever（排水）是 sewer 与 sewage 共同的远祖。

abstract.en: Picture a dark stream sliding along a brick tunnel under a busy street.
abstract.cn: 想象一条暗色的水流，沿着热闹街道下方的砖砌隧道向前滑行。

abstract.en: See a drain mouth pouring grey water onto the sand at low tide.
abstract.cn: 想象退潮时一个排水口把灰色水流倒在沙滩上。

abstract.en: Watch clear water leave a plant while the dirt is squeezed into a thick cake.
abstract.cn: 想象清水从处理厂流出，而污物被压成厚厚的一块泥饼。

examples.en: The city built a new plant to treat its sewage.
examples.cn: 这座城市新建了一座处理污水的工厂。

examples.en: Raw sewage was leaking from a broken pipe near the school.
examples.cn: 未经处理的污水正从学校附近的破裂管道中渗出。

examples.en: Scientists test the river water for signs of sewage each week.
examples.cn: 科学家每周检测河水，看是否有污水混入的迹象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「水渍」——污水流过总要留下水渍；这是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 exaqua（排水）→ 古法语 essuever（排水）→ 英语 sewer（下水道）→ sewer + 法语词尾 -age（成堆之物）→ sewage（污水）。

sensesIntro.en: Sewage starts as the collective dirty water removed by sewers, widens to the waste it carries, and then serves engineering and figurative uses.
sensesIntro.cn: sewage 先指被下水道收走的脏水整体，再扩大到其中携带的污物，随后进入工程与比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark flow moving along a buried pipe, out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股暗色水流沿着埋在地下的管道流动，不为人所见。

branches.en: The waste water carried by drains is the central sense.
branches.cn: 由管道排走的废水是核心义项。

branches.en: The solid waste in the same flow is the material side of the word.
branches.cn: 同一条水流里的固态污物，是这个词的物质层面。

branches.en: The plant entry is the engineering sense, where flow is measured.
branches.cn: 进厂污水是工程义，讲究的是一股可计量的流量。

branches.en: Once it reaches open water, sewage becomes a named source of pollution.
branches.cn: 一旦进入开放水体，污水就成了有名字的污染源。

branches.en: The literal flow supplies the image of a system washing harm out of sight.
branches.cn: 字面上的污水流，为「把害处冲走藏起」的比喻提供了画面。

intro.en: Sewage is built from the noun sewer and the French-derived suffix -age, a pattern shared by luggage, mileage, and drainage.
intro.cn: sewage 由名词 sewer 与源自法语的词尾 -age 构成，同样的模式也见于 luggage、mileage 与 drainage。

latinIntro.en: The core of both sewer and sewage is Latin exaqua, to drain water away, which French reshaped into the verb essuever.
latinIntro.cn: sewer 与 sewage 的核心是拉丁语 exaqua（把水排走），法语将它改写为动词 essuever。

items.example: The prefix ex- points to water being taken out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 表示把水带出去。

items.example: Aqua gives the water element of the word.
items.exampleCN: aqua 为这个词提供「水」这个意义元素。

items.example: Exaqua is the deepest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: exaqua 是这个词族最深的一层。

items.example: Essuever reshapes the Latin verb for French use.
items.exampleCN: essuever 把拉丁语动词改写成法语形式。

items.example: Sewer names the channel itself.
items.exampleCN: sewer 指管道本身。

items.example: The suffix -age turns a thing into the mass of that thing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 把单个事物变成一堆该事物。

items.meaning: the waste water carried by sewers
items.example: Sewage is the mass that sewers carry.
items.exampleCN: sewage 就是下水道所输送的那一团东西。

items.example: Sewerage refers to the system, sewage to the flow.
items.exampleCN: sewerage 指体系，sewage 指污水流。

items.example: Drainage shows the same -age pattern in action.
items.exampleCN: drainage 正好展示了同样的 -age 构词模式。

definition_zh: 下水道；污水管；缝制者；缝纫工
definition_en: an underground pipe that carries away waste water and rain water, or, from the verb sew, a person who stitches things
core_image: 城市脚下一条暗渠，脏水在里面打着旋往外流
scene: 雨夜里，街角的井盖咕嘟冒水。After the storm, the old sewer overflowed into the street.
sceneCN: 这里 sewer 是「下水道」（第 1 个义项：排放污水的暗管）；句意：暴雨过后，那条老下水道的水漫上了街道。

pos.zh: 缝制者；缝纫工（由动词 sew 加 -er 构成）

derivatives.zh: 有下水道设施的
污水；污物（sewer 的变体形式，旧法语 seuwiere 同源）
下水道系统；污水处理（sewer 加 -age 后缀，该词历史上受过 sewage 拼写影响）

senses.title: An underground channel for waste water
senses.definition: an underground pipe or channel that carries away dirty water and waste from homes and streets
senses.definitionCN: 把住宅与街道的脏水和废物排走的地下管道或暗渠
senses.example: The city is replacing its crumbling sewer.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市正在更换老朽的下水道。
senses.why: Old French seuwiere meant a channel that drains water, and the draining image is still the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 seuwiere 指排水的沟渠，排水这个画面至今仍是这个词的核心。

senses.title: The pipe itself
senses.definition: the pipe itself, made of concrete, clay, or plastic, rather than the channel as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 指管道本身（混凝土、陶土或塑料制），而不是整条渠道
senses.example: A crack in the sewer lets tree roots creep in.
senses.exampleCN: 污水管上的一道裂缝让树根钻了进来。
senses.why: When people talk about materials, joints, and repairs, the channel becomes the object that can split and leak.
senses.whyCN: 当人们谈论材质、接口和维修时，渠道就变成了会开裂、会渗漏的实物。

senses.title: A drain for rainwater
senses.definition: a public drain that takes away storm water as well as dirty water
senses.definitionCN: 同时排走雨水与脏水的公共排水设施
senses.example: The storm sewer was built to handle heavy summer rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这条雨水下水道是为了应对夏季暴雨而建的。
senses.why: Draining was the original job, so the word stretched from waste alone to any water that must be carried off.
senses.whyCN: 排水本来就是它最初的职能，所以词义从只排废物扩展到一切需要带走的水。

senses.title: A person who sews
senses.definition: a person whose job is to stitch cloth and make clothes
senses.definitionCN: 以缝纫布料、制作衣服为职业的人
senses.example: She worked for years as a sewer in a coat factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家大衣厂做了多年缝纫工。
senses.why: The verb sew takes the agent suffix -er, so a sewer is literally one who sews, a completely separate history.
senses.whyCN: 动词 sew 加上施动后缀 -er，所以 sewer 字面上就是「缝东西的人」，这是完全不同的另一条来源。

senses.title: A dressmaker, a dated and regional use
senses.titleCN: 女装裁缝；缝衣匠（旧用、方言用）
senses.definition: a dressmaker or a person who makes garments, an old and regional sense
senses.definitionCN: 裁缝或做衣服的人，属于旧用法与地域用法
senses.example: In the old ledger she is listed as a sewer of fine linen.
senses.exampleCN: 在这本旧账簿里，她被记为缝制细麻布衣的裁缝。
senses.why: Farming and town records named trades by the tool used, so sewing work gave people the title of sewer.
senses.whyCN: 农事与城镇档案常按所用工具称呼行当，所以缝纫活儿就给了人们 sewer 这个称呼。

intro.en: Sewer, the drain, comes from Old French seuwiere, a channel that drains water, which is usually traced to Latin ex + aqua, out of the water.
intro.cn: sewer（下水道）来自古法语 seuwiere（排水的渠道），一般认为可追溯到拉丁语 ex（出）+ aqua（水），即「把水排出去」。

items.en: The verb exaquare is usually reconstructed from ex, out, plus aqua, water, and describes draining water away.
items.cn: 一般认为 exaquare 由 ex（出）与 aqua（水）构成，意思是把水排走。

items.en: A reconstructed noun such as exaquarium, a place where water is drawn off, is often proposed as the link.
items.cn: 常有人提出重构名词 exaquarium（排水之处）作为中间环节。

items.en: Seuwiere means a drain or channel for carrying water, and it passes into English.
items.cn: seuwiere 意为排水沟渠，这个词进入英语。

items.en: Sewer first names a drain or an outfall for water in English texts.
items.cn: 中古英语文献中，sewer 最初指排水沟或出水口。

items.en: Modern cities build covered sewers, and the word settles on the underground pipe of the water closet and storm drain.
items.cn: 近代城市修建带盖的下水道，这个词固定指厕所与雨水排放所用的地下管道。

items.en: The homograph sewer, a person who sews, comes separately from the verb sew and is unrelated.
items.cn: 同形的 sewer（缝纫者）另自动词 sew 派生，与下水道无关。

note.en: Sewer is the pipe that carries water away, while its neighbours name the water, the system, or the stitcher.
note.cn: sewer 是把水带走的管道，而它的邻居分别指污水、整个系统，或者缝纫的人。

entries.definition: the dirty water and waste carried by sewers
entries.definitionCN: 下水道里输送的污水与污物（sewer 的同源变体）

entries.definition: the network of sewers and the system of handling waste water
entries.definitionCN: 下水道网络与污水处理系统（sewer 加 -age）

entries.definition: a person who sows seeds, only looks and sounds like sewer and has a different root
entries.definitionCN: 播种的人；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a pipe or channel that carries water away from a place
entries.definitionCN: 排水管；下水道

entries.definition: a narrow channel at the roadside that collects rain water
entries.definitionCN: 路边的雨水沟；檐槽

entries.definition: a covered channel that carries water under a road
entries.definitionCN: 道路下方的涵洞；暗渠

normalIntro.en: Sewer belongs to the water family of aqua, and it echoes drain, gutter, and culvert down the street.
normalIntro.cn: sewer 属于 aqua（水）这个词族，在街面下与 drain、gutter、culvert 互相呼应。

normal.en: A sewer carries water away, which matches the old idea of water drawn out.
normal.cn: sewer 把水带走，正合「把水排出去」的老意思。

normal.en: Remember the pair: sewer is the pipe, sewage is what flows in it.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：sewer 是管子，sewage 是管子里流的东西。

normal.en: Sewerage with -age names the whole system, just as mileage names a length.
normal.cn: 带 -age 的 sewerage 指整套系统，就像 mileage 指里程。

normal.en: The homograph sewer from sew means a stitcher, so context decides.
normal.cn: 来自动词 sew 的同形词 sewer 指缝纫者，要看上下文判断。

normal.en: Storm sewer drains rain, sanitary sewer drains household waste.
normal.cn: storm sewer 排雨水，sanitary sewer 排生活污水。

abstract.en: Picture a dark tunnel under the pavement with a current of grey water.
abstract.cn: 想象人行道下面一条黑暗的隧道，里面淌着灰色的水。

abstract.en: Imagine a manhole cover lifting a little under heavy rain.
abstract.cn: 想象暴雨中井盖被水顶得微微抬起。

abstract.en: Think of a seamstress bent over a needle: this sewer stitches cloth, not water.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女工俯身在针线前：这个 sewer 缝的是布，不是水。

examples.en: Workers found a blocked sewer under the main road.
examples.cn: 工人在主路下面发现了一条堵塞的下水道。

examples.en: The plant sends its waste into a treatment sewer.
examples.cn: 这家工厂把废液排入一条处理用下水道。

examples.en: My grandmother was a sewer in a small clothing workshop.
examples.cn: 我祖母曾在一家小服装作坊当缝纫工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「苏娥」——苏娥每天清早钻进井口，替整条街通下水道；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex（出）+ aqua（水）→ 重构形式 exaquare（排水）→ 古法语 seuwiere（排水渠）→ 英语 sewer（下水道）；另由动词 sew + 施动后缀 -er 构成同形的「缝纫者」。

sensesIntro.en: Sewer starts as the channel that drains water, narrows to the pipe itself, widens to storm drains, and then meets an unrelated homograph meaning a stitcher.
sensesIntro.cn: sewer 从「排水的渠道」出发，收窄到「管道本身」，再扩展到「雨水下水道」，最后遇到一个无关的同形词「缝纫者」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark channel under the street that carries water away.
core.cn: 核心意象：街道下方一条把水带走的暗渠。

branches.en: The original drain sense keeps the image whole.
branches.cn: 原始的「排水渠道」义保留完整画面。

branches.en: The sense narrows to the physical pipe that can crack.
branches.cn: 义项收窄到会开裂的实体管道。

branches.en: Rain water extends the drain idea to public storm drains.
branches.cn: 雨水把排水概念扩展到公共雨水下水道。

branches.en: A different root, the verb sew, gives the separate stitching senses.
branches.cn: 另一条来源动词 sew 给出独立的缝纫义项。

branches.en: All three water senses rest on the same hidden channel.
branches.cn: 三个与水的义项都立足于同一条隐藏渠道。

intro.en: Sewer is built from the Latin pair ex and aqua, and English extends it to sewage and sewerage.
intro.cn: sewer 由拉丁语的 ex 与 aqua 组成，英语又扩展出 sewage 与 sewerage。

latinIntro.en: Latin aqua means water, and ex means out; together they describe water being drawn off.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aqua 意为水，ex 意为出去，合起来表示把水排走。

items.example: Ex- in exaquare marks water going out.
items.exampleCN: exaquare 中的 ex- 表示水往外流。

items.example: Aqua is the ancient root of the water image.
items.exampleCN: aqua 是水里意象的古老词根。

items.example: Exaquare is usually given as the source of the French word.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为 exaquare 是法语词的源头。

items.meaning: a drain, a channel for water
items.example: Seuwiere is the direct French source of sewer.
items.exampleCN: seuwiere 是 sewer 的直接法语来源。

items.example: The suffix -er marks the pipe in sewer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 在这里标出「管道」身份。

items.meaning: a system or a collected whole
